title.en: Volume 351 Biographies 110: Zhao Tingzhi, Zhang ShangYing, Liu Zhengfu, He Zhizhong, Zheng Juzhong, An Yaochen, Zhang Kangguo, Zhu E, Liu Kui, Lin Shu, Guan Shiren, Hou Meng
title.raw: 卷三百五十一 列傳第一百一十 趙挺之 張商英 劉正夫 何執中 鄭居中 安堯臣 張康國 朱諤 劉逵 林攄 管師仁 侯蒙 Volume 351 Biographies 110: Zhao Tingzhi, Zhang ShangYing, Liu Zhengfu, He Zhizhong, Zheng Juzhong, An Yaochen, Zhang Kangguo, Zhu E, Liu Kui, Lin Shu, Guan Shiren, Hou Meng

sentences.zh: 趙挺之

translations.literal: Zhao Tingzhi
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingzhi

sentences.zh: 趙挺之，字正夫，密州諸城人。

translations.literal: Zhao Tingzhi, courtesy name Zhengfu, was a native of Zhucheng in Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingzhi, styled Zhengfu, was from Zhucheng in Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 進士上第。

translations.literal: He attained the upper tier of the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the top rank.

sentences.zh: 熙寧建學，選教授登、棣二州，通判德州。

translations.literal: When schools were established in the Xining era, he was selected as professor in Deng and Di Prefectures, and served as vice-prefect of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining educational reforms, he was appointed professor in Deng and Di prefectures and then served as assistant prefect of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，賜士卒緡錢，郡守貪耄不時給，卒怒譟，持白梃突入府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, cash was granted to soldiers. The prefect, greedy and decrepit, failed to disburse it promptly. The soldiers grew angry and clamored, and with white staves in hand stormed into the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong came to the throne, the court granted cash payments to the troops. The prefect, both greedy and senile, delayed distribution. Enraged, the soldiers raised a clamor and charged into the yamen wielding white clubs.

sentences.zh: 守趨避，左右盡走。

translations.literal: The prefect rushed to flee; all his attendants scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect fled in haste, and every attendant fled with him.

sentences.zh: 挺之坐堂上，呼問狀，立發庫錢，而治其為首者，眾即定。

translations.literal: Tingzhi sat in the hall, summoned them to ask the circumstances, immediately released treasury funds, and punished the ringleaders; the crowd at once settled.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi remained seated in the hall, called them forward to hear their grievances, promptly opened the treasury to pay them, and punished the ringleaders. The disturbance ended at once.

sentences.zh: 魏境河屢決，議者欲徙宗城縣，轉運使檄挺之往視，挺之云：「縣距高原千歲矣，水未嘗犯。

translations.literal: In Weizhou the river repeatedly burst its banks. Those debating the issue wished to relocate Zongcheng County. The transport commissioner ordered Tingzhi to go inspect. Tingzhi said: "The county has stood on high ground for a thousand years; the water has never harmed it.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Wei border the river broke its dikes again and again. Some officials proposed moving Zongcheng County. The transport commissioner dispatched Tingzhi to inspect the site. He reported: "That county has stood on high ground for a millennium; floodwaters have never touched it.

sentences.zh: 今所遷不如舊，必為民害。

translations.literal: The place now proposed for relocation is inferior to the old site; it will surely harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: The proposed new site is worse than the old one; moving there would only bring harm to the people.

sentences.zh: 」使者卒徙之，財二年，河果壞新城，漂居民略盡。

translations.literal: The envoy ultimately moved it. In less than two years, the river indeed destroyed the new city and swept away nearly all the residents.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy moved the county anyway. Within two years the river devastated the new town and swept away nearly all its inhabitants.

sentences.zh: 召試館職，為秘閣校理，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: Summoned for an examination for a post in the institutes, he became collator in the Secret Archive, and was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled for a qualifying examination for an archival post, he was appointed collator in the Secret Archive and later promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 初，挺之在德州，希意行市易法。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Tingzhi was in Dezhou, he curried favor by enforcing the market-trade law.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving in Dezhou, Tingzhi had ingratiated himself by zealously enforcing Wang Anshi's market-trade monopoly.

sentences.zh: 黃庭堅監德安鎮，謂鎮小民貧，不堪誅求。

translations.literal: Huang Tingjian supervised Dean garrison and said the garrison was small and the people poor, unable to bear exactions.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Tingjian, who oversaw Dean garrison, argued that the community was too small and its people too poor to endure such exactions.

sentences.zh: 及召試，蘇軾曰：「挺之聚斂小人，學行無取，豈堪此選。

translations.literal: When the examination was held, Su Shi said: "Tingzhi is a petty man who amasses wealth by exaction; in learning and conduct he has nothing worth taking — how could he be fit for this selection?
translations.idiomatic: At the examination Su Shi declared: "Tingzhi is an extortionate sycophant with no learning or integrity to speak of. He is unworthy of this appointment.

sentences.zh: 」至是，劾奏軾草麻有云「民亦勞止」，以為誹謗先帝。

translations.literal: At this time he impeached Su Shi, noting that in drafting an edict he had written "the people too have wearied," taking this as slander of the former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion he impeached Su Shi, citing the phrase "the people too have grown weary" in a draft edict as defamation of the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 既而坐不論蔡確，通判徐州，俄知楚州。

translations.literal: He was then found guilty for failing to speak out against Cai Que, was made vice-prefect of Xuzhou, and soon became prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently punished for not denouncing Cai Que, demoted to assistant prefect of Xuzhou, and soon after appointed prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為國子司業，歷太常少卿，權吏部侍郎，除中書舍人、給事中。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as vice-director of the Directorate of Education, served successively as vice-minister of rites, acting vice-minister of personnel, and was appointed as a drafter in the Secretariat and supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as vice-director of the Directorate of Education, then served as vice-minister of rites, acting vice-minister of personnel, and was finally appointed drafter in the Secretariat and supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 使遼，遼主嘗有疾，不親宴，使近臣即館享客。

translations.literal: On a mission to Liao, the Liao ruler had been ill and did not preside at banquets in person; he had close ministers receive guests at the embassy.
translations.idiomatic: On an embassy to Liao, he found the Liao ruler ill and unable to host banquets in person; courtiers were sent to the embassy to receive the guests instead.

sentences.zh: 比歲享乃在客省，與諸國等，挺之始爭正其禮。

translations.literal: In recent years the receptions had been held in the guest office, on equal footing with other states; Tingzhi was the first to insist on correcting the protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years those receptions had been held in the guest office, treating the Song envoy no differently from emissaries of lesser states. Tingzhi was the first to insist that the proper rites be restored.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended, he served as vice-minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took the throne, Tingzhi was appointed vice-minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 哲宗祔廟，議遷宣祖，挺之言：「上於哲宗兄弟，同一世；

translations.literal: When Zhezong was enshrined in the ancestral temple, there was debate over relocating Xuanzu. Tingzhi said: "Your Majesty and Zhezong were brothers of the same generation;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong was enshrined in the ancestral temple, officials debated moving the tablet of Emperor Xuanzu. Tingzhi argued: "Your Majesty and Emperor Zhezong were brothers of the same generation;

sentences.zh: 宣祖未當遷。

translations.literal: Xuanzu ought not be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzu ought not be displaced.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: They followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 拜御史中丞，為欽聖后陵儀仗使。

translations.literal: He was appointed censor-in-chief and made director of the Empress Dowager Qinsheng's funerary procession.
translations.idiomatic: He was made censor-in-chief and director of the funerary procession for Empress Dowager Qinsheng.

sentences.zh: 曾布以使事聯職，知禁中密指，諭使建議紹述，於是挺之排擊元祐諸人不遺力。

translations.literal: Zeng Bu, linked to Tingzhi through a mission, knew the secret intent within the palace and urged him to propose restoring former policies; thereupon Tingzhi attacked the Yuanyou faction without sparing effort.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu, who had served with him on an embassy and knew the secret signals from within the palace, urged him to propose reviving the late emperor's reforms. Tingzhi then attacked the Yuanyou faction with unrestrained zeal.

sentences.zh: 由吏部尚書拜右丞，進左丞、中書門下侍郎。

translations.literal: From minister of personnel he was appointed right vice grand councilor, advanced to left vice grand councilor and vice-governor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from minister of personnel to right vice grand councilor, then to left vice grand councilor and vice-governor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 時蔡京獨相，帝謀置右輔，京力薦挺之，遂拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: At that time Cai Jing served alone as chief councilor. The emperor planned to appoint a right-hand assistant; Cai strongly recommended Tingzhi, and he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing then held the chancellorship alone. When the emperor sought a second chief minister, Cai vigorously recommended Tingzhi, who was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 既相，與京爭雄，屢陳其姦惡，且請去位避之。

translations.literal: Once he became chief councilor, he contended with Cai Jing for dominance, repeatedly exposed Cai's wickedness, and asked to leave office to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he openly vied with Cai Jing, repeatedly denouncing his corruption and asking to resign rather than share power with him.

sentences.zh: 以觀文殿大學士、中太一宮使留京師。

translations.literal: He was retained in the capital as academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in the capital with the titles of academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace.

sentences.zh: 乞歸青州，將入辭，會彗星見，帝默思咎徵，盡除京諸蠹法，罷京，召見挺之曰：「京所為，一如卿言。

translations.literal: He requested to return to Qingzhou. About to enter for farewell audience, a comet appeared. The emperor silently reflected on this omen of guilt, abolished all of Cai Jing's pernicious laws, dismissed Cai, summoned Tingzhi and said: "What Cai Jing did was just as you said.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to return to Qingzhou. As he was about to take leave, a comet appeared. The emperor read it as a sign of wrongdoing, swept away Cai Jing's ruinous policies, dismissed Cai, and summoned Tingzhi. "Everything Cai Jing did," he said, "was just as you warned.

sentences.zh: 」加挺之特進，仍為右僕射。

translations.literal: Tingzhi was granted special advancement and again served as right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi was given special advancement and retained as Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 京在崇寧初，首興邊事，用兵連年不息。

translations.literal: Cai Jing at the start of the Chongning era had first raised border affairs; warfare continued year after year without cease.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongning reign Cai Jing had first stirred up border conflict, and war dragged on without pause.

sentences.zh: 帝臨朝，語大臣曰：「朝廷不可與四夷生隙，隙一開，禍不解，兵民肝腦塗地，豈人主愛民恤物意哉！

translations.literal: The emperor held court and told the chief ministers: "The court must not create rifts with the four barbarians. Once a rift opens, disaster cannot be resolved; soldiers and people smear the ground with their guts and brains — is this the sovereign's intent to cherish the people and care for life!
translations.idiomatic: At court the emperor told his ministers: "We must not pick quarrels with the surrounding peoples. Once a breach is opened, catastrophe cannot easily be closed; men die and provinces bleed — is that what a ruler who loves his people intends?

sentences.zh: 」挺之退謂同列曰：「上志在息兵，吾曹所宜將順。

translations.literal: Tingzhi withdrew and told his colleagues: "The emperor's intent is to end warfare; we ought to follow and support it.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Tingzhi told his colleagues: "The emperor means to halt the wars. We should align ourselves with that intent.

sentences.zh: 」已而京復相，挺之仍以大學士使佑神觀。

translations.literal: Before long Cai Jing again became chief councilor; Tingzhi was again made academician and commissioner of the Youshen Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Cai Jing returned to power, and Tingzhi was sent back to the Youshen Abbey as academician-in-residence.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒，諡曰「清憲」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Defender-in-Chief; his posthumous title was "Pure and Law-abiding."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Defender-in-Chief with the posthumous name "Pure and Law-abiding."

sentences.zh: 張商英

translations.literal: Zhang Shangying
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shangying

sentences.zh: 張商英，字天覺，蜀州新津人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shangying, courtesy name Tianjue, was a native of Xinjin in Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shangying, styled Tianjue, was from Xinjin in Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 長身偉然，姿采如峙玉。

translations.literal: Tall and imposing in stature, his bearing was like standing jade.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and commanding, his bearing like a pillar of jade.

sentences.zh: 負氣俶儻，豪視一世。

translations.literal: Full of spirit and free and easy, he looked upon the age with bold contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and untrammeled, he regarded the world with audacious contempt.

sentences.zh: 調通川主簿。

translations.literal: He was appointed registry clerk of Tongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He began as registry clerk of Tongchuan.

sentences.zh: 渝州蠻叛，說降其酋。

translations.literal: When the Yizhou tribes rebelled, he persuaded their chief to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes of Yizhou rose in revolt, he persuaded their chieftain to surrender.

sentences.zh: 辟知南川縣。

translations.literal: He was invited to serve as magistrate of Nanchuan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited to serve as magistrate of Nanchuan County.

sentences.zh: 章惇經制夔夷，狎侮郡縣吏，無敢與共語。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun was overseeing the Qiang-Yi region, treating contemptuously the prefectural and county officials; none dared speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun, charged with pacifying the Qiang and Yi territories, treated local officials with open contempt; none dared even speak to him.

sentences.zh: 部使者念獨商英足抗之，檄至夔。

translations.literal: The circuit commissioner considered that only Shangying could stand up to him, and summoned him to Kui with an order.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit commissioner felt that only Shangying could stand up to him and summoned him to Kui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 惇詢人才，使者以商英告，即呼入同食。

translations.literal: Dun inquired about talented men; the commissioner named Shangying, and Dun immediately called him in to eat together.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun asked after able men, the commissioner named Shangying, and Zhang Dun at once summoned him to share a meal.

sentences.zh: 商英著道士服，長揖就坐。

translations.literal: Shangying wore Daoist robes, bowed with clasped hands, and took his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Shangying appeared in Daoist garb, made a deep bow, and took his seat.

sentences.zh: 惇肆意大言，商英隨機折之，落落出其上。

translations.literal: Dun spoke brazenly at length; Shangying rebutted him as occasion arose, clearly rising above him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun spoke grandly and without restraint; Shangying parried him point by point and plainly held the upper hand.

sentences.zh: 惇大喜，延為上客。

translations.literal: Dun was greatly pleased and received him as an honored guest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun was delighted and treated him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 歸，薦諸王安石，因召對，以檢正中書禮房擢監察御史。

translations.literal: On returning, he recommended him to Wang Anshi. Summoned for audience, he was promoted from adjuster in the Zhongshu ritual section to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: On returning home he recommended Shangying to Wang Anshi. Summoned for imperial audience, Shangying was promoted from adjuster in the Zhongshu ritual section to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 臺獄失出劫盜，樞密檢詳官劉奉世駁之，詔糾察司劾治。

translations.literal: The censorate and judicial office mistakenly released robbers; Liu Fengshi, reviewing officer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, rejected the judgment; the emperor ordered the inspection office to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate and judicial office had wrongly released some robbers; Liu Fengshi of the Bureau of Military Affairs reversed the ruling, and the emperor ordered the inspectorate to investigate.

sentences.zh: 商英奏：「此出大臣私忿，願收還主柄，使耳目之官無為近臣所脅。

translations.literal: Shangying memorialized: "This arises from a senior minister's private resentment. I beg that authority be restored so that the organs of surveillance are not coerced by close courtiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shangying memorialized: "This case stems from a senior minister's private grievance. I ask that real authority be restored so the watchdog offices are no longer bullied by favorites at court.

sentences.zh: 」神宗為置不治。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the matter set aside without punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong ordered the matter dropped.

sentences.zh: 商英遂言奉世庇博州失入囚，因摭院吏徇私十二事，語侵樞臣，於是文彥博等上印求去。

translations.literal: Shangying then said Fengshi had shielded a wrongly admitted prisoner in Bozhou, and listed twelve instances of yamen clerks showing partiality. His words impugned the military councilors, whereupon Wen Yanbo and others submitted their seals and asked to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Shangying then charged that Fengshi had protected a wrongly convicted prisoner in Bozhou, citing twelve cases of clerical favoritism that implicated the military councilors. Wen Yanbo and others thereupon submitted their seals and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 詔責商英監荊南稅，更十年，乃得館閣校勘、檢正刑房。

translations.literal: An edict punished Shangying by making him supervisor of taxes in Jingnan. After another ten years he obtained posts as collator in the institutes and adjuster in the penal section.
translations.idiomatic: Shangying was demoted to supervise taxes in Jingnan. Ten years passed before he was again appointed collator in the institutes and adjuster in the penal section.

sentences.zh: 商英嘗薦舒亶可用，至是，亶知諫院，商英以婿王溈之所業示之，亶繳奏，以為事涉干請，責監赤岸鹽稅。

translations.literal: Shangying had once recommended Shu Dan as suitable. At this time Dan was director of the remonstrance bureau. Shangying showed him his son-in-law Wang Weizhi's examination essays; Dan forwarded them in memorial, deeming the matter involved improper solicitation, and Shangying was punished by supervising salt taxes at Chian.
translations.idiomatic: Shangying had once recommended Shu Dan. Now that Shu Dan headed the remonstrance bureau, Shangying showed him examination essays by his son-in-law Wang Weizhi. Shu Dan reported the favor-seeking to the throne, and Shangying was demoted to supervise salt taxes at Chian.

sentences.zh: 哲宗初，為開封府推官，屢詣執政求進。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhezong's reign he was investigative officer of the Kaifeng prefecture, and repeatedly visited the chief administrators seeking advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhezong's reign he served as investigative officer in the Kaifeng prefecture and repeatedly lobbied the chief ministers for promotion.

sentences.zh: 朝廷稍更新法之不便於民者，商英上書言：「『三年無改於父之道，可謂孝矣。

translations.literal: The court gradually revised New Policies inconvenient to the people. Shangying submitted a memorial saying: "'If for three years one does not change his father's way, it may be called filial.
translations.idiomatic: As the court gradually amended the New Policies that had burdened the people, Shangying memorialized: "'If for three years one does not alter his father's ways, that may be called filial.'

sentences.zh: 』今先帝陵土未乾，即議變更，得為孝乎？

translations.literal: Now the former emperor's tomb earth is not yet dry, yet change is already debated — can this be filial?
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's tomb is scarcely settled, yet we already speak of change — where is the filial piety in that?

sentences.zh: 」且移書蘇軾求入臺，其廋詞有「老僧欲住烏寺，嗬佛罵祖」之語。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Su Shi seeking entry into the censorate; its cryptic words included "an old monk wishing to stay at Crow Temple, shouting at the Buddha and cursing the patriarch."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Su Shi seeking a censorate appointment; the veiled wording included the line "an old monk wishing to lodge at Crow Temple, hollering at the Buddha and reviling the patriarchs."

sentences.zh: 呂公著聞之，不悅。

translations.literal: When Lü Gongzhu heard of it, he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gongzhu heard of this and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 出提點河東刑獄，連使河北、江西、淮南。

translations.literal: He was sent out as judicial intendant of Hedong, and served in succession as commissioner in Hebei, Jiangxi, and Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as judicial intendant of Hedong, then served successive terms as commissioner in Hebei, Jiangxi, and Huainan.

sentences.zh: 哲宗親政，召為右正言、左司諫。

translations.literal: When Zhezong took personal rule, he was summoned as right rectifier and left remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong assumed personal rule, Shangying was recalled as right rectifier and left remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 商英積憾元祐大臣不用己，極力攻之，上疏曰：「先帝盛德大業，跨絕今古，而司馬光、呂公著、劉摯、呂大防援引朋儔，敢行譏議。

translations.literal: Shangying nursed resentment that Yuanyou chief ministers had not employed him, and attacked them with utmost force. He submitted a memorial saying: "The former emperor's great virtue and achievement surpass all ages past and present, yet Sima Guang, Lü Gongzhu, Liu Zhi, and Lü Dafang drew in their faction and dared to launch ridicule and criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Harboring resentment that the Yuanyou ministers had ignored him, Shangying attacked them relentlessly. He memorialized: "The late emperor's virtue and achievement stand above all history, yet Sima Guang, Lü Gongzhu, Liu Zhi, and Lü Dafang rallied their faction and dared to mock and undermine his legacy.

sentences.zh: 凡詳定局之所建明，中書之所勘當，戶部之所行遣，百官之所論列，詞臣之所作命，無非指擿抉揚，鄙薄嗤笑，翦除陛下羽翼於內，擊逐股肱於外，天下之勢，岌岌殆矣。

translations.literal: Whatever the Detailed Examination Bureau proposed, the Secretariat examined, the Ministry of Revenue dispatched, the hundred officials debated, or the drafters composed in edicts — all was nothing but pointing out flaws, prying them open, exposing them, despising, sneering, cutting away Your Majesty's wings within and driving out your arms and legs without; the empire's situation was perilously precarious.
translations.idiomatic: Every measure from the Detailed Examination Bureau, every ruling from the Secretariat, every order from the Ministry of Revenue, every debate among officials, every edict from the drafting office — all was turned into occasions for nitpicking, mockery, and scorn. They clipped your wings within the palace and drove your able ministers from office. The realm stood on the brink of ruin.

sentences.zh: 今天青日明，誅賞未正，願下禁省檢索前後章牘，付臣等看詳，簽揭以上，陛下與大臣斟酌而可否焉。

translations.literal: Now the sky is azure and the sun bright; rewards and punishments are not yet made right. I hope Your Majesty will order the palace offices to gather the memorials before and after, hand them to us for examination, affix and submit them upward, and let Your Majesty and the chief ministers consider and approve or reject.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Heaven's favor has returned, rewards and punishments remain unsettled. I ask that the palace offices gather all relevant memorials, send them to us for review, and submit our findings so that Your Majesty and your ministers may decide what to accept or reject.

sentences.zh: 」遂論內侍陳衍以搖宣仁，至比之呂、武；

translations.literal: He then criticized the eunuch Chen Yan for shaking Xuanren, even comparing him to Lü and Wu;
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked the eunuch Chen Yan for undermining Empress Dowager Xuanren, even comparing her to Empress Lü and Empress Wu;

sentences.zh: 乞追奪光、公著贈諡，仆碑毀塚；

translations.literal: he asked to revoke the posthumous titles of Guang and Gongzhu, topple their steles and destroy their tombs;
translations.idiomatic: he called for stripping Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu of their posthumous honors, toppling their steles and demolishing their tombs;

sentences.zh: 言文彥博背負國恩，及蘇軾、范祖禹、孫升、韓川諸人，皆相繼受譴。

translations.literal: he said Wen Yanbo had betrayed the state's grace, and Su Shi, Fan Zuyu, Sun Sheng, Han Chuan and others all successively suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: he denounced Wen Yanbo for ingratitude; Su Shi, Fan Zuyu, Sun Sheng, Han Chuan, and others were punished in turn.

sentences.zh: 又言：「願陛下無忘元祐時，章惇無忘汝州時，安燾無忘許昌時，李清臣、曾布無忘河陽時。

translations.literal: He further said: "May Your Majesty not forget the Yuanyou era; may Zhang Dun not forget his time in Ruzhou; may An Yan not forget his time in Xuchang; may Li Qingchen and Zeng Bu not forget their time in Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He also warned: "Let Your Majesty not forget the Yuanyou years; let Zhang Dun not forget his exile in Ruzhou; let An Yan not forget his banishment in Xuchang; let Li Qingchen and Zeng Bu not forget their days in Heyang.

sentences.zh: 」其觀望捭闔，以險語激怒當世，概類此。

translations.literal: His watchfulness, maneuvering, and use of dangerous words to provoke the age were generally of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: In watching the wind, shifting sides, and goading contemporaries with inflammatory language, he was much the same.

sentences.zh: 惇、燾交惡，商英欲助惇，求所以傾燾者。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun and An Yan were mutually hostile. Shangying wished to help Dun and sought a means to overthrow Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun and An Yan were at odds. Shangying, seeking to aid Zhang Dun, looked for a way to bring An Yan down.

sentences.zh: 陽翟民蓋氏養子漸，先為祖母所逐，以家資屬其女，經元豐訴理不得直。

translations.literal: In Yangdi, a man of the Gai clan named Jian had been adopted. First driven out by his grandmother, the family property was given to her daughter. Through the Yuanfeng era he sued for justice without redress.
translations.idiomatic: In Yangdi, an adopted son of the Gai clan named Jian had been cast out by his grandmother, who passed the family estate to her daughter. Since the Yuanfeng era he had sued without obtaining justice.

sentences.zh: 商英論其冤，導漸使遮執政，及詣御史府訐燾姻家與蓋女為道地。

translations.literal: Shangying argued his injustice, directed Jian to intercept the chief administrators, and had him go to the censorate to accuse Yan's affinal kin of colluding with Gai's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Shangying took up his cause, coached Jian to waylay the chief ministers, and sent him to the censorate to accuse An Yan's in-laws of colluding with Gai's daughter.

sentences.zh: 哲宗不直商英，徙左司員外郎。

translations.literal: Zhezong did not side with Shangying and transferred him to left outer bureau vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong rejected Shangying's account and transferred him to left outer bureau vice-director.

sentences.zh: 既與漸交關事皆露，責監江寧酒。

translations.literal: Once his dealings with Jian were exposed, he was punished by supervising wine in Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: When his conspiracy with Jian came to light, he was demoted to supervise wine sales in Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 起知洪州，為江淮發運副使，入權工部侍郎，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was raised to serve as prefect of Hongzhou, became vice commissioner of the Jiang-Huai transport, entered the capital as acting vice-minister of works, and was promoted to drafter in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed prefect of Hongzhou, then vice transport commissioner on the Jiang-Huai route, acting vice-minister of works in the capital, and finally drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 謝表歷詆元祐諸賢，眾益畏其口。

translations.literal: In his letter of thanks he repeatedly slandered the Yuanyou worthies; the multitude feared his mouth all the more.
translations.idiomatic: In his letter of thanks he launched fresh attacks on the Yuanyou worthies, and people feared his tongue all the more.

sentences.zh: 徽宗出為河北都轉運使，降知隨州。

translations.literal: Under Huizong he was sent out as chief transport commissioner of Hebei, then demoted to prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huizong he was first sent out as chief transport commissioner of Hebei, then demoted to prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初，為吏部、刑部侍郎，翰林學士。

translations.literal: At the start of Chongning he served as vice-minister of personnel and punishment, and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongning reign he served as vice-minister of personnel and punishment and as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 蔡京拜相，商英雅與之善，適當制，過為褒美。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing became chief councilor, Shangying had been on good terms with him; as the drafter of the appointment edict, he praised him excessively.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing became chief councilor, Shangying, who had long been on good terms with him, drafted an appointment edict that lavished excessive praise.

sentences.zh: 尋拜尚書右丞，轉左丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, then transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Right Vice Director, then Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 復與京議政不合，數詆京「身為輔相，志誌在逢君」，御史以為非所宜言，且取商英所作《元祐嘉禾頌》及司馬光《祭文》，斥其反覆。

translations.literal: Again his policy discussions with Cai Jing did not agree; he repeatedly denounced Jing: "Though you are chief minister, your ambition is merely to flatter the ruler." The censors considered this an improper thing to say, and also produced Shangying's "Ode to the Yuanyou Auspicious Grain" and his elegy for Sima Guang to expose his reversals.
translations.idiomatic: He again clashed with Cai Jing in policy and repeatedly accused him of "being chief minister in title only while seeking only to flatter the emperor." Censors deemed this improper and cited Shangying's own "Ode to the Yuanyou Auspicious Grain" and his elegy for Sima Guang to expose his hypocrisy.

sentences.zh: 罷知亳州，入元祐黨籍。

translations.literal: He was dismissed to serve as prefect of Bozhou and entered the Yuanyou faction register.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed to Bozhou and enrolled in the register of Yuanyou partisans.

sentences.zh: 京罷相，削籍知鄂州。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing left the chancellorship, Shangying was stricken from the register and made prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing fell from power, Shangying was removed from the partisan register and appointed prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 京復相，以散官安置歸、峽兩州。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing again became chief councilor, he was settled as a commoner in Gui and Xia Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing returned to office, Shangying was reduced to commoner status and confined to Gui and Xia prefectures.

sentences.zh: 大觀四年，京再逐，起知杭州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daguann, when Cai Jing was again driven out, he was raised to serve as prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daguann, after Cai Jing was ousted again, Shangying was appointed prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 過闕賜對，奏曰：「神宗修建法度，務以去大害、興大利，今誠一一舉行，則盡紹述之美。

translations.literal: Passing through the capital he was granted audience and memorialized: "Emperor Shenzong established laws and institutions, aiming to remove great harms and establish great benefits. If they are now truly carried out one by one, the full beauty of restoring his policies will be realized.
translations.idiomatic: On passing through the capital he was granted audience and said: "Emperor Shenzong's laws were meant to remove grave evils and bring great benefits. Carry them out faithfully and the full glory of the late emperor's reforms will be restored.

sentences.zh: 法若有弊，不可不變，但不失其意足矣。

translations.literal: If the laws have flaws, they cannot but be changed, but it is enough not to lose their intent.
translations.idiomatic: If a law has defects it must be amended — but only so long as its original purpose is preserved.

sentences.zh: 」留為資政殿學士、中太一宮使。

translations.literal: He was retained as academician of the Hall of Utmost Governance and commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was retained in the capital as academician of the Hall of Utmost Governance and commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace.

sentences.zh: 頃之，除中書侍郎，遂拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed vice-governor of the Secretariat, and then Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made vice-governor of the Secretariat, then Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 京久盜國柄，中外怨疾，見商英能立同異，更稱為賢，徽宗因人望相之。

translations.literal: Cai Jing had long stolen state power; within and without all resented and despised him. Seeing that Shangying could establish differences, they again called him worthy; Huizong appointed him chief councilor because of public esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing had long monopolized power, and resentment ran deep inside and outside court. When people saw that Shangying was willing to dissent, they praised him as a worthy man, and Huizong made him chief councilor to satisfy public expectation.

sentences.zh: 時久旱，彗星中天，是夕，彗不見，明日，雨。

translations.literal: At the time there had been long drought; a comet crossed the zenith. That evening the comet disappeared; the next day, rain.
translations.idiomatic: The land had suffered long drought, and a comet crossed the meridian. That night the comet vanished; the next day rain fell.

sentences.zh: 徽宗喜，大書「商霖」二字賜之。

translations.literal: Huizong rejoiced and in large characters wrote the two characters "Shang's Rain" and bestowed them on him.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong rejoiced and in large characters bestowed on him the two characters "Shang's Rain" — rain sent by Shangying.

sentences.zh: 商英為政持平，謂京雖明紹述，但借以劫制人主，禁錮士大夫爾。

translations.literal: Shangying's governance was even-handed. He said that though Cai Jing openly restored former policies, he only used them to coerce the ruler and imprison the scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shangying governed even-handedly. He held that although Cai Jing had preached "restoration of the late emperor's reforms," he had used that banner mainly to control the emperor and muzzle the literati.

sentences.zh: 於是大革弊事，改當十錢以平泉貨，復轉般倉以罷直達，行鈔法以通商旅，蠲橫斂以寬民力。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly reformed corrupt practices: changed the value-ten coins to stabilize currency, restored the transport granaries to abolish direct shipment, implemented note law to ease merchants and travelers, and remitted irregular levies to relax the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: He then launched broad reforms: reformed the ten-cash coins to stabilize currency, restored transport granaries to end direct shipment, enacted note law to free trade, and cancelled arbitrary levies to ease the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 勸徽宗節華侈，息土木，抑僥幸。

translations.literal: He urged Huizong to restrain luxury, halt construction projects, and suppress favor-seeking.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Huizong to curtail extravagance, halt construction projects, and restrain undue favoritism.

sentences.zh: 帝頗嚴憚之，嘗葺升平樓，戒主者遇張丞相導騎至，必匿匠樓下，過則如初。

translations.literal: The emperor feared him considerably. Once while repairing the Shengping Tower, he instructed the overseer that when Vice Director Zhang's escort arrived, craftsmen must hide beneath the tower and resume only after he passed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to regard him with real caution. Once, while renovating the Shengping Tower, he instructed the overseer that whenever Chancellor Zhang's escort appeared, the craftsmen must hide below the tower and only resume work after he had passed.

sentences.zh: 楊戩除節度使，商英曰：「祖宗之法，內侍無至團練使。

translations.literal: Yang Jian was appointed military commissioner. Shangying said: "By the law of our ancestors, inner attendants do not rise even to regimental training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was appointed military commissioner, Shangying objected: "By ancestral precedent, eunuchs should not rise even to regimental training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 有勳勞當陟，則別立昭宣、宣政諸使以寵之，未聞建旄鉞也。

translations.literal: When one with merit and service deserves promotion, they establish separate envoys such as Zhaoxuan and Xuanzheng to honor him — I have never heard of granting banner and battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: When someone with merit deserved promotion, the court might create special envoys like the Zhaoxuan or Xuanzheng commissioners to honor him — but Shangying had never heard of granting a full military commission with banner and axe.

sentences.zh: 」訖持不下，論者益稱之。

translations.literal: He held firm to the end and would not yield; commentators praised him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He held his ground to the end and would not back down, and commentators praised him all the more.

sentences.zh: 然意廣才疏，凡所當為，先於公坐誦言，故不便者得預為計。

translations.literal: Yet his ambitions were broad and his talents limited; whatever he intended to do, he would announce aloud in open session first, so those who opposed him could prepare countermeasures in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his ambitions outran his abilities: whatever he meant to do, he would announce aloud in open session first, so those who stood to lose could prepare their countermeasures in advance.

sentences.zh: 何執中、鄭居中日夜釀織其短，先使言者論其門下客唐庚，竄之惠州。

translations.literal: He Zhizhong and Zheng Juzhong worked day and night weaving together charges against him; they first had memorialists attack his client Tang Geng and exile him to Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhizhong and Zheng Juzhong worked day and night to weave charges against him, first having memorialists attack his client Tang Geng and banish him to Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 有郭天信者，以方技隸太史，徽宗潛邸時，嘗言當履天位，自是稍睠寵之。

translations.literal: There was one Guo Tianxin, who served in the Directorate of Astronomy by virtue of divination skills; when Huizong was still heir apparent, he had once predicted that Huizong would ascend the throne, and from then on received a measure of favor.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Guo Tianxin, who served in the Directorate of Astronomy through divination and technical arts. When Huizong was still heir apparent, he had once predicted that Huizong would ascend the throne, and from then on enjoyed a measure of imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 商英因僧德洪、客彭几與語言往來，事覺，鞫於開封府。

translations.literal: Shangying had been exchanging words with the monk Dehong and a client Peng Ji; when this came to light, the case was tried at the Kaifeng prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: Shangying had been exchanging words with the monk Dehong and a client named Peng Ji. When this came to light, the case was tried at the Kaifeng prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞張克公疏擊之，以觀文殿大學士知河南府，旋貶崇信軍節度副使，衡州安置。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Kegong submitted a memorial attacking him; Shangying was made Grand Master of the Hall for Viewing Literature and prefect of Henan, then soon demoted to vice military commissioner of Chongxin Circuit and placed under supervision at Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Kegong submitted a memorial attacking him. Shangying was made Grand Master of the Hall for Viewing Literature and prefect of Henan, then soon demoted to vice military commissioner of Chongxin Circuit and placed under supervision at Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 天信亦斥死。

translations.literal: Tianxin was also expelled and died.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tianxin was also expelled and died.

sentences.zh: 京遂復用。

translations.literal: Jing was then restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing was then restored to office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，太學諸生誦商英之冤，京懼，乃乞令自便。

translations.literal: Before long, students of the Imperial Academy proclaimed Shangying's innocence; Jing grew fearful and requested permission to retire on his own terms.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, students of the Imperial Academy were proclaiming Shangying's innocence. Jing grew fearful and asked permission to retire on his own terms.

sentences.zh: 繼復還故官職。

translations.literal: Later he was restored to his former posts.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shangying was restored to his former posts.

sentences.zh: 宣和三年卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuanhe he died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Xuanhe, at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 商英作相，適承蔡京之後，小變其政，譬饑者易為食，故蒙忠直之名。

translations.literal: When Shangying served as chancellor, he succeeded directly after Cai Jing and made modest changes to his policies — like a hungry man finding any food easy to accept — and thus earned a reputation for integrity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: When Shangying served as chancellor, he came directly after Cai Jing and made modest changes to his policies. To a hungry man any food is welcome — and so he earned a reputation for integrity and uprightness.

sentences.zh: 靖康褒表司馬光、范仲淹，而商英亦贈太保。

translations.literal: At Jingkang, Sima Guang and Fan Zhongyan were honored and enshrined, and Shangying likewise received the posthumous title of Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingkang, Sima Guang and Fan Zhongyan were honored and enshrined; Shangying too received the posthumous title of Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 紹興中，又賜諡「文忠」，天下皆不謂然。

translations.literal: During the Shaoxing era, he was further granted the posthumous epithet Wenzhong; people everywhere considered it undeserved.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoxing era he was further granted the posthumous epithet Wenzhong, and people everywhere considered it undeserved.

sentences.zh: 兄：唐英。

translations.literal: Elder brother: Tang Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother: Tang Ying.

sentences.zh: 兄 唐英

translations.literal: Elder brother Tang Ying
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Tang Ying

sentences.zh: 唐英，字次功。

translations.literal: Tang Ying, style name Cigong.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Ying, whose style name was Cigong.

sentences.zh: 少攻苦讀書，至經歲不知肉味。

translations.literal: In youth he studied diligently, to the point that for entire years he did not know the taste of meat.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied with fierce dedication, to the point that for whole years he scarcely knew the taste of meat.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，翰林學士孫抃得其《正議》五十篇，以為馬周、魏元忠不足多。

translations.literal: After passing the jinshi examination, Hanlin Academician Sun Bian obtained his fifty chapters of Correct Discourses and judged that Ma Zhou and Wei Yuanzhong scarcely deserved mention by comparison.
translations.idiomatic: After he passed the jinshi examination, Hanlin Academician Sun Bian obtained his fifty chapters of Correct Discourses and judged that even Ma Zhou and Wei Yuanzhong scarcely deserved mention by comparison.

sentences.zh: 薦試賢良方正，不就。

translations.literal: He was recommended for the examination of worthies and upright men, but declined.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for the examination of worthies and upright men, he declined.

sentences.zh: 調穀城令。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Gucheng County.

sentences.zh: 縣圃歲畦薑，貸種與民，還其陳，復配賣取息，銓曹指為富縣。

translations.literal: The county garden planted ginger annually; seeds were loaned to the people, old stock was recovered, and they were sold again at interest — the Bureau of Appointments marked it a wealthy county.
translations.idiomatic: The county garden planted ginger every year: seeds were loaned to the people, old stock was recovered, and the ginger was sold again at interest. The Bureau of Appointments marked Gucheng a wealthy county.

sentences.zh: 唐英至，空其圃，植千株柳，作柳亭其中，聞者諮羨。

translations.literal: When Tang Ying arrived, he cleared the garden, planted a thousand willows, and built a willow pavilion within it; those who heard of it sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Ying arrived, he cleared the garden, planted a thousand willows, and built a willow pavilion among them. Those who heard of it sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 英宗繼大統，唐英上《謹始書》云：「為人後者為子，懼他日必有引漢定陶故事以惑宸聽者，願杜其漸。

translations.literal: When Yingzong succeeded to the throne, Tang Ying submitted a Book on Being Careful at the Start, saying: One who becomes another's heir becomes a son; I fear that someday someone will cite the Han precedent of Dingtao to mislead the imperial ear — I pray Your Majesty will cut off such inclinations at the root.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong succeeded to the throne, Tang Ying submitted a Book on Being Careful at the Start, saying: "One who becomes another's heir becomes a son. I fear that someday someone will cite the Han precedent of Dingtao to mislead the imperial ear. I pray Your Majesty will cut off such inclinations at the root."

sentences.zh: 」既而濮議果起。

translations.literal: Before long, the dispute over the title of the deceased Emperor Pu did indeed arise.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, the dispute over the title of the deceased Emperor Pu did indeed arise.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，皇太后垂簾，又上書請立潁王為皇太子。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill, the Empress Dowager held court from behind the curtain; Tang Ying submitted another memorial requesting that Prince Ying be established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill and the Empress Dowager held court from behind the curtain, Tang Ying submitted another memorial requesting that Prince Ying be established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，知其人，擢殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, recognizing his talent, he was promoted to palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong ascended the throne, recognizing his talent, he promoted Tang Ying to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 入對，帝問何尚衣綠，對曰：「前者固得之，回授臣父。

translations.literal: In audience, the emperor asked why he still wore green robes; he replied: I had rightly earned it earlier, but transferred it to my father.
translations.idiomatic: In audience, the emperor asked why he still wore green robes. He replied: "I had rightly earned it earlier, but transferred it to my father."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉其孝，賜五品服。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his filial piety and granted him fifth-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his filial piety and granted him robes of the fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 帝方厲精圖治，急於用人，唐英言：「知江寧府王安石經術道德，宜在陛下左右。

translations.literal: The emperor was vigorously striving to govern well and eager to employ talent; Tang Ying said: Wang Anshi, prefect of Jiangning, possesses both classical learning and moral integrity — he ought to serve at Your Majesty's side.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was vigorously striving to govern well and eager to employ talent. Tang Ying said: "Wang Anshi, prefect of Jiangning, possesses both classical learning and moral integrity. He ought to serve at Your Majesty's side."

sentences.zh: 」又論宗室祿多費鉅，宜以服為差殺；

translations.literal: He also argued that the stipends for imperial clansmen consumed vast sums and ought to be scaled according to rank of dress;
translations.idiomatic: The man also argued that the stipends for imperial clansmen consumed vast sums and ought to be scaled according to rank of dress;

sentences.zh: 天下苦差役不均，盍思所以寬民力、代民勞者。

translations.literal: that the realm groaned under unequal corvée levies, and that the court should devise means to lighten the people's burdens and labor on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: and that the realm groaned under unequal corvée levies, so the court should devise means to lighten the people's burdens and labor on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 其後略施行。

translations.literal: These proposals were later implemented in part.
translations.idiomatic: Some of these proposals were later put into practice.

sentences.zh: 帝方欲用之，以父憂去，未幾卒。

translations.literal: The emperor was just about to employ him when he departed to observe mourning for his father; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was just about to employ him when he departed to observe mourning for his father. Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 唐英有史材，嘗著《仁宗政要》、《宋名臣傳》、《蜀檮杌》，行於世。

translations.literal: Tang Ying had talent for historiography and had written Essentials of Renzong's Governance, Biographies of Eminent Song Ministers, and The Shu Pestle, all of which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Ying had a gift for historiography. He wrote Essentials of Renzong's Governance, Biographies of Eminent Song Ministers, and The Shu Pestle, all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 劉正夫

translations.literal: Liu Zhengfu
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengfu

sentences.zh: 劉正夫，字德初，衢州西安人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhengfu, style name Dechu, a native of Xi'an in Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengfu, style name Dechu, was a native of Xi'an in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 未冠入太學，有聲，與范致虛、吳材、江嶼號「四俊」。

translations.literal: Before reaching adulthood he entered the Imperial Academy and gained renown; with Fan Zhixu, Wu Cai, and Jiang Yu he was called the Four Talents.
translations.idiomatic: Before reaching adulthood he entered the Imperial Academy and gained renown. With Fan Zhixu, Wu Cai, and Jiang Yu he was called the Four Talents.

sentences.zh: 元豐八年，南省奏名在優選，而犯高魯王諱，凡五人皆當黜。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanfeng, when provincial examination results were reported, he ranked among the top candidates but violated the taboo name of Prince Gao of Lu; all five such candidates were liable for dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanfeng, when provincial examination results were reported, he ranked among the top candidates but violated the taboo name of Prince Gao of Lu. All five such candidates were liable for dismissal.

sentences.zh: 宣仁后曰：「外家私諱頒未久，不可以妨寒士。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren said: The private taboo of our maternal clan has only lately been promulgated — we cannot let it bar poor scholars from advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren said: "The private taboo of our maternal clan has only lately been promulgated. We cannot let it bar poor scholars from advancement."

sentences.zh: 」命置末級。

translations.literal: She ordered them placed at the lowest rank.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered that they be placed at the lowest rank.

sentences.zh: 久之，為太學錄、太常博士。

translations.literal: After some time he served as recorder of the Imperial Academy and erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he served as recorder of the Imperial Academy and erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 母服闋，御史中丞石豫薦之，召赴闕，道除左司諫。

translations.literal: When his mourning for his mother ended, Censor-in-Chief Shi Yu recommended him; summoned to court, he was appointed on the road Left Remonstrance Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning for his mother ended, Censor-in-Chief Shi Yu recommended him. Summoned to court, he was appointed on the road to Left Remonstrance Clerk.

sentences.zh: 時方究蔡邸獄，正夫入對，徽宗語及之，徐引淮南「尺布、斗粟」之謠以對。

translations.literal: At the time the case of Prince Cai's household was under investigation; in audience Zhengfu, when Huizong spoke of it, gently cited the Huainan proverb about a foot of cloth and a dipper of grain in reply.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the case of Prince Cai's household was under investigation. In audience, when Huizong spoke of it, Zhengfu gently cited the Huainan proverb about "a foot of cloth, a dipper of grain" in reply.

sentences.zh: 帝感動，解散其獄，待蔡王如初。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved, dissolved the case, and treated Prince Cai as before.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, the emperor dissolved the case and treated Prince Cai as before.

sentences.zh: 他日，謂正夫曰：「兄弟之間，人所難言，卿獨能及此，後必為公輔。

translations.literal: On another day he told Zhengfu: Among brothers, what men find hardest to speak of — you alone have managed it; hereafter you will surely become a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On another day he told Zhengfu: "Among brothers, what men find hardest to speak of — you alone have managed it. Hereafter you will surely become a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「元祐、紹聖所修《神宗史》，互有得失，當折中其說，傳信萬世。

translations.literal: He also said: The History of Shenzong compiled in the Yuanyou and Shaosheng eras each has its merits and faults; their accounts should be reconciled and made trustworthy for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The History of Shenzong compiled in the Yuanyou and Shaosheng eras each has its merits and faults. Their accounts should be reconciled and made trustworthy for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 」遂詔刊定，而以起居舍人為編修官。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to revise and fix the text, with the diarist as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued to revise and fix the text, appointing the diarist as compiler.

sentences.zh: 不閱月，遷中書舍人，進給事中、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Within less than a month he was transferred to drafting secretary, then advanced to supervisory censor and vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In under a month he was transferred to drafting secretary, then advanced to supervisory censor and vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 蔡京據相位，正夫欲附翼之，奏言：「近命官纂錄紹述先志及施行政事，願得陳力其間。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing held the chancellorship, Zhengfu wished to attach himself to his wings and memorialized: Your Majesty has recently ordered officials to compile records of the continuation of the late emperor's will and the implementation of governance; I wish to offer my strength in this work.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing held the chancellorship, Zhengfu wished to attach himself to his faction and memorialized: "Your Majesty has recently ordered officials to compile records of the continuation of the late emperor's will and the implementation of governance. I wish to offer my strength in this work."

sentences.zh: 」詔俾閱詳焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to review and examine the project.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him to review and examine the project.

sentences.zh: 京罷，正夫又與鄭居中陰援京。

translations.literal: When Jing was dismissed, Zhengfu again secretly supported him together with Zheng Juzhong.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing was dismissed, Zhengfu again secretly supported him together with Zheng Juzhong.

sentences.zh: 京憾劉逵次骨，而逵善正夫，京雖賴其助，亦惡之。

translations.literal: Jing hated Liu Kui to the marrow, yet Liu Kui was friendly toward Zhengfu; although Jing relied on Zhengfu's help, he also detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing hated Liu Kui to the marrow, yet Liu Kui was friendly toward Zhengfu. Although Jing relied on Zhengfu's help, he also detested him.

sentences.zh: 因章綖鑄錢獄辭及正夫，時使遼還，京諷有司追逮之。

translations.literal: Through testimony in the case of Zhang Yan's coin counterfeiting, Zhengfu was implicated; he was returning from an embassy to Liao when Jing hinted to the authorities to pursue and arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: Through testimony in the case of Zhang Yan's coin counterfeiting, Zhengfu was implicated. He was returning from an embassy to Liao when Jing hinted to the authorities to pursue and arrest him.

sentences.zh: 帝知其情，第貶兩秩。

translations.literal: The emperor understood the situation and merely demoted him two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the situation, the emperor merely demoted him two ranks.

sentences.zh: 京又出之成都，入辭，留為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Jing then had him sent out to Chengdu; on presenting farewell respects, he was retained as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Jing then had him sent out to Chengdu. On presenting farewell respects, he was retained as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 京愈不能平，謀中以事。

translations.literal: Jing grew ever more resentful and plotted to entrap him in a matter.
translations.idiomatic: Jing grew ever more resentful and plotted to entrap him.

sentences.zh: 作春宴樂語，有「紫宸朝罷袞衣閑」之句，京黨張康國密白帝曰：「袞衣豈可閑？

translations.literal: Composing festive verse for a spring banquet, he included the line After court at Zichen, the imperial robes lie idle; Jing's ally Zhang Kangguo secretly informed the emperor: How can the imperial robes lie idle?
translations.idiomatic: Composing festive verse for a spring banquet, he included the line "After court at Zichen, the imperial robes lie idle." Jing's ally Zhang Kangguo secretly informed the emperor: "How can the imperial robes lie idle?"

sentences.zh: 」竟改龍圖閣直學士、知河南府。

translations.literal: In the end he was changed to academician directly attached to the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and made prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was made academician directly attached to the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 召為工部尚書，拜右丞，進中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was recalled as minister of works, appointed vice director, and advanced to vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The man was recalled as minister of works, appointed vice director, and advanced to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太學諸生習樂成，京欲官之。

translations.literal: When students of the Imperial Academy completed their music training, Jing wished to grant them official posts.
translations.idiomatic: Once students of the Imperial Academy completed their music training, Jing wished to grant them official posts.

sentences.zh: 正夫曰：「朝廷長育人材，規為時用，而使與伶官齒，策名以是，得無為士子羞乎？

translations.literal: Zhengfu said: The court nurtures talent for service to the age — to rank them alongside entertainers as their path to office, would that not bring shame upon scholars?
translations.idiomatic: Zhengfu said: "The court nurtures talent for service to the age. To rank them alongside entertainers as their path to office — would that not bring shame upon scholars?"

sentences.zh: 」東封儀物已具，正夫請間，力陳不可，帝皆為之止，益喜其不與京同。

translations.literal: The ritual paraphernalia for the eastern sacrifice had already been prepared; Zhengfu requested a private audience and forcefully argued against it — the emperor halted each plan and came to delight all the more that he was not of one mind with Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual paraphernalia for the eastern sacrifice had already been prepared. Zhengfu requested a private audience and forcefully argued against it. The emperor halted each plan and came to delight all the more that he was not of one mind with Jing.

sentences.zh: 政和六年，擢拜特進、少宰。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenghe he was promoted to specially advanced and Junior Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenghe he was promoted to specially advanced rank and Junior Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 才半歲，屬疾，三上章告老，除安化軍節度使、開府儀同三司致仕。

translations.literal: Only half a year later he fell ill; thrice submitting memorials requesting retirement, he was granted the posts of military commissioner of Anhua Circuit and Honorary Grand Master with ceremonials equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Only half a year later he fell ill. Thrice submitting memorials requesting retirement, he was granted the posts of military commissioner of Anhua Circuit and Honorary Grand Master with ceremonials equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 病小愈，丐東歸，詔肩輿至內殿，長子皁民掖入坐。

translations.literal: When his illness eased slightly, he begged leave to return east; an edict summoned him by sedan chair to the inner hall, where his eldest son Zaomin supported him in to be seated.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness eased slightly, he begged leave to return east. An edict summoned him by sedan chair to the inner hall, where his eldest son Zaomin supported him in to be seated.

sentences.zh: 從容及燕雲事，曰：「臣起書生，軍旅之事未之學，然兩朝信誓之久，四海生靈之眾，願深留聖思。

translations.literal: At leisure he touched on the Yan-Yun question, saying: Your subject rose from the ranks of scholars and has never studied military affairs, yet the long-standing sworn faith between two courts and the countless lives across the realm — I pray Your Majesty will weigh these deeply in your thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: At leisure he touched on the Yan-Yun question, saying: "Your subject rose from the ranks of scholars and has never studied military affairs. Yet the long-standing sworn faith between two courts and the countless lives across the realm — I pray Your Majesty will weigh these deeply in your thoughts."

sentences.zh: 」明日，徙節安靜軍，起充中太一宮使，封康國公。

translations.literal: The next day he was transferred to Anjing Circuit, reappointed commissioner of the Zhongtaiyi Palace, and enfeoffed as Duke of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day he was transferred to Anjing Circuit, reappointed commissioner of the Zhongtaiyi Palace, and enfeoffed as Duke of Kang.

sentences.zh: 將行，賜之詩及硯筆、圖畫、藥餌、香茶之屬甚厚。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, the emperor bestowed upon him poems, inkstones and brushes, paintings, medicines, fragrant tea, and many other gifts in great abundance.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, the emperor bestowed poems, inkstones and brushes, paintings, medicines, fragrant tea, and many other gifts in great abundance.

sentences.zh: 正夫獻詩謝，帝又屬和以榮其歸。

translations.literal: Zhengfu presented a poem in thanks; the emperor also composed a matching verse to honor his return home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengfu presented a poem in thanks. The emperor also composed a matching verse to honor his return home.

sentences.zh: 至盱眙，病亟，命子弟作遺牘，自書「留神根本，深戒持盈」八字，遂卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: Reaching Xuyi, his illness grew critical; he ordered his sons to draft a final memorial and personally wrote the eight characters Keep the root in mind; deeply guard against excess, then died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Xuyi, his illness grew critical. He ordered his sons to draft a final memorial and personally wrote the eight characters "Keep the root in mind; deeply guard against excess," then died, aged fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，諡「文憲」，再贈太傅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Guardian, given the epithet Wenxian, and later posthumously granted Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The man was posthumously granted Grand Guardian, given the epithet Wenxian, and later posthumously granted Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 正夫由博士入都，馴致宰相，能迎時上下，持祿養權。

translations.literal: Zhengfu entered the capital from an erudite post and gradually reached the chancellorship; he could trim his sails to suit the times and used his salary to nourish his power.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengfu entered the capital from an erudite post and gradually reached the chancellorship. He could trim his sails to suit the times and used his salary to nourish his power.

sentences.zh: 性吝嗇，惟恐不足於財。

translations.literal: By nature he was stingy and ever anxious that his wealth might not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Stingy by nature, he was ever anxious that his wealth might not suffice.

sentences.zh: 晚年，築第杭州萬松嶺，以建閣奉御書為名，悉取其旁軍營民舍，議者譏之。

translations.literal: In his later years he built a mansion on Wansong Ridge in Hangzhou, naming it for a pavilion built to house imperial calligraphy; he took over all the adjacent military camps and civilian dwellings, and critics mocked him for it.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he built a mansion on Wansong Ridge in Hangzhou, naming it for a pavilion built to house imperial calligraphy. He took over all the adjacent military camps and civilian dwellings, and critics mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 帝眷念不衰，以皁民為兵部侍郎；

translations.literal: The emperor's favor never waned; Zaomin was made vice minister of war;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's favor never waned. Zaomin was made vice minister of war;

sentences.zh: 少子阜民，徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: his younger son Fumin, a drafter of the Huayou Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: his younger son Fumin was made a drafter of the Huayou Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 何執中

translations.literal: He Zhizhong
translations.idiomatic: He Zhizhong

sentences.zh: 何執中，字伯通，處州龍泉人。

translations.literal: He Zhizhong, style name Botong, a native of Longquan in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhizhong, style name Botong, was a native of Longquan in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 進士高第，調台、亳二州判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination with high marks and was appointed judicial administrator in Taizhou and Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The man passed the jinshi examination with high marks and was appointed judicial administrator in Taizhou and Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 亳數易守，政不治。

translations.literal: Bozhou changed prefects frequently and governance went untended.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhou changed prefects frequently, and governance went untended.

sentences.zh: 曾鞏至，頗欲振起之，顧諸僚無可仗信者，執中一見合意，事無纖鉅，悉委以剸決。

translations.literal: When Zeng Gong arrived, he wished greatly to revive administration but found none among the staff he could trust; at first meeting He Zhizhong pleased him, and matters great and small were all entrusted to his decisive judgment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Gong arrived, he wished greatly to revive administration but found none among the staff he could trust. At first meeting He Zhizhong pleased him, and matters great and small were all entrusted to his decisive judgment.

sentences.zh: 有妖獄久不竟，株連寢多。

translations.literal: A sorcery case had long gone unresolved, with the net of implication growing ever wider.
translations.idiomatic: A sorcery case had dragged on unresolved, with the net of implication growing ever wider.

sentences.zh: 執中訊諸囚，聽其相與語，謂牛羊之角皆曰「股」，扣其故，閉不肯言，而相視色變。

translations.literal: He Zhizhong interrogated the prisoners and listened as they spoke among themselves; they all called cattle and goats' horns thighs — when pressed for the reason, they closed their mouths and would not speak, but glanced at one another with changed expressions.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhizhong interrogated the prisoners and listened as they spoke among themselves. They all called cattle and goats' horns "thighs." When pressed for the reason, they closed their mouths and would not speak, but glanced at one another with changed expressions.

sentences.zh: 執中曰：「是必為師張角諱耳。

translations.literal: He Zhizhong said: This must be evasion of the name of Master Zhang Jue.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhizhong said: "This must be evasion of the name of Master Zhang Jue."

sentences.zh: 」即扣頭引伏。

translations.literal: At once they kowtowed and confessed.
translations.idiomatic: They immediately kowtowed and confessed.

sentences.zh: 蔣之奇使淮甸，號強明，官吏望風震懾，見執中喜曰：「一州六邑，賴有君爾。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhiqi served on the Huai region commission, renowned for severity; officials trembled at his approach — meeting He Zhizhong he said with pleasure: One prefecture and six counties have relied on you alone.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhiqi served on the Huai region commission, renowned for severity. Officials trembled at his approach. Meeting He Zhizhong, he said with pleasure: "One prefecture and six counties have relied on you alone."

sentences.zh: 」知海鹽縣，為政識後先，邑人紀其十異。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Haiyan he governed with a sense of priorities; the townspeople recorded ten unusual acts of his rule.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Haiyan he governed with a sense of priorities. The townspeople recorded ten unusual acts of his rule.

sentences.zh: 蔡京籍上書人為邪等，初無朝覲及入都之禁，執中申言之，且請任在京職秩者皆罷遣。

translations.literal: Cai Jing registered memorial submitters as heterodox, but at first there was no ban on court appearances or entry into the capital; He Zhizhong brought this forward and requested that all those holding office ranks in the capital be dismissed and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing registered memorial submitters as heterodox, but at first there was no ban on court appearances or entry into the capital. He Zhizhong brought this forward and requested that all those holding office ranks in the capital be dismissed and sent away.

sentences.zh: 辟雍成，執中請開學殿，使都人士女縱觀，大為士論所貶。

translations.literal: When the Imperial Academy was completed, He Zhizhong requested that the study hall be opened so men and women of the capital could freely watch — greatly condemned in scholarly opinion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial Academy was completed, He Zhizhong requested that the study hall be opened so men and women of the capital could freely watch. This was greatly condemned in scholarly opinion.

sentences.zh: 崇寧四年，拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongning he was appointed Vice Director of the Right in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongning he became Vice Director of the Right in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 大觀初，進中書、門下侍郎，積官金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the start of the Daguan era he advanced to vice director of the Secretariat and vice director of the Chancellery, cumulatively reaching Grand Master of the Golden Purple and Bright Tally.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daguan era he advanced to vice director of the Secretariat and vice director of the Chancellery, cumulatively reaching Grand Master of the Golden Purple and Bright Tally.

sentences.zh: 一意謹事京，三年，遂代為尚書左丞，加特進。

translations.literal: Single-mindedly serving Jing with care, after three years he replaced him as Vice Director of the Left and was given specially advanced rank.
translations.idiomatic: Single-mindedly serving Jing with care, after three years he replaced him as Vice Director of the Left and was given specially advanced rank.

sentences.zh: 制下，太學諸生陳朝老詣闕上書曰：「陛下知蔡京姦，解其相印，天下之人鼓舞，有若更生。

translations.literal: When the appointment decree was issued, Imperial Academy student Chen Chaolao went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial saying: Your Majesty recognized Cai Jing's wickedness and removed his seal of chancellor — people throughout the realm exulted as though reborn.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment decree was issued, Imperial Academy student Chen Chaolao went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty recognized Cai Jing's wickedness and removed his seal of chancellor. People throughout the realm exulted as though reborn.

sentences.zh: 及相執中，中外默然失望。

translations.literal: Yet when He Zhizhong was made chancellor, court and countryside alike fell silent in disappointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when He Zhizhong was made chancellor, court and countryside alike fell silent in disappointment.

sentences.zh: 執中雖不敢肆為非法若京之蠹國害民，然碌碌庸質，初無過人。

translations.literal: Although He Zhizhong dared not openly commit outrages like Jing's national ruin and harm to the people, he was a plodding mediocrity with nothing extraordinary about him.
translations.idiomatic: Although He Zhizhong dared not openly commit outrages like Jing's ruin of the state and harm to the people, he was a plodding mediocrity with nothing extraordinary about him.

sentences.zh: 天下敗壞至此，如人一身，髒府受沴已深，豈庸庸之醫所能起乎？

translations.literal: The realm's ruin has reached this pass — like a human body whose vital organs have been deeply afflicted; how can a commonplace physician possibly cure it?
translations.idiomatic: The realm's ruin has reached this pass — like a human body whose vital organs have been deeply afflicted. How can a commonplace physician possibly cure it?

sentences.zh: 執中夤緣攀附，致位二府，亦已大幸，遽俾之經體贊元，是猶以蚊負山，多見其不勝任也。

translations.literal: He Zhizhong climbed by connections and attachment to reach the Two Departments — already great fortune — yet to be charged at once with steering the state and assisting the sovereign is like asking a mosquito to carry a mountain; one need only look to see he is unequal to the task.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhizhong climbed by connections and attachment to reach the Two Departments — already great fortune. Yet to charge him at once with steering the state and assisting the sovereign is like asking a mosquito to carry a mountain. One need only look to see he is unequal to the task.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏不省，而眷注益異。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not heeded; yet imperial favor toward him grew ever more extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went unheeded, yet imperial favor toward him grew ever more extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 初，賜第信陵坊，以為淺隘，更徙金順坊甲第。

translations.literal: At first he was granted a residence in Xinling Ward; finding it cramped, he was moved to a grand mansion in Jinshun Ward.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was granted a residence in Xinling Ward. Finding it cramped, he was moved to a grand mansion in Jinshun Ward.

sentences.zh: 建嘉會成功閣，帝親書钜額以示寵。

translations.literal: He built the Jiahui Chenggong Pavilion; the emperor personally wrote a large plaque to show his favor.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Jiahui Chenggong Pavilion, and the emperor personally wrote a large plaque to show his favor.

sentences.zh: 執中與蔡京並相，凡營立皆預議，略無所建明。

translations.literal: He Zhizhong served as chancellor alongside Cai Jing; he took part in deliberations on every undertaking but offered scarcely any constructive proposals of his own.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhizhong served as chancellor alongside Cai Jing. He took part in deliberations on every undertaking but offered scarcely any constructive proposals of his own.

sentences.zh: 及張商英任事，執中惡其出己上，與鄭居中合擠之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shangying took charge of affairs, He Zhizhong resented his rise above him and joined Zheng Juzhong in squeezing him out.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shangying took charge of affairs, He Zhizhong resented his rise above him and joined Zheng Juzhong in squeezing him out.

sentences.zh: 陳瓘在台州，執中起遷人石悈知州事，使脅取《尊堯集》，謀必死瓘，瓘不死，執中怒罷悈。

translations.literal: Chen Guan was in Taizhou. He Zhizhong promoted the banished official Shi Jie to administer the prefecture and had him coerce the surrender of Respect for Yao; he plotted to ensure Chen Guan's death. When Chen Guan did not die, He Zhizhong angrily dismissed Shi Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guan was in Taizhou. He Zhizhong promoted the banished official Shi Jie to administer the prefecture and had him coerce the surrender of Respect for Yao, plotting to ensure Chen Guan's death. When Chen Guan did not die, He Zhizhong angrily dismissed Shi Jie.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，大長公主喪，罷上元端門觀燈，執中言：「不宜以長主故閼眾情，願特為徙日，以昭與民同樂之意。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, during mourning for the Grand Eldest Princess, the lantern viewing at the Duan Gate on the fifteenth was canceled. He Zhizhong said: It is not fitting to suppress the people's wishes because of the princess's mourning. I pray Your Majesty will specially move the date, to show the intent of sharing joy with the people.
