He Zhizhong said: "It is not fitting to suppress the people's wishes because of the princess's mourning. I pray Your Majesty will specially move the date, to show the intent of sharing joy with the people."

sentences.zh: 」帝重逆其請，為申五日期。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly went against his own wishes and granted a postponement of five days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly went against his own wishes and granted a postponement of five days.

sentences.zh: 用提舉修《哲宗史紀》恩，加少保。

translations.literal: By grace for supervising the compilation of the Annals of Emperor Zhezong, he was promoted to Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: By grace for supervising the compilation of the Annals of Emperor Zhezong, he was promoted to Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 入宴太清樓，錫白玉帶。

translations.literal: He attended a banquet at the Taiqing Tower and was granted a white jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: He attended a banquet at the Taiqing Tower and was granted a white jade belt.

sentences.zh: 會正宰相官名，轉少傅，為太宰；

translations.literal: When the chancellor's titles were regularized, he was transferred to Junior Tutor and made Grand Chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: When the chancellor's titles were regularized, he was transferred to Junior Tutor and made Grand Chancellor;

sentences.zh: 又遷少師，封榮國公。

translations.literal: he was further promoted to Junior Preceptor and enfeoffed as Duke of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: he was further promoted to Junior Preceptor and enfeoffed as Duke of Rong.

sentences.zh: 執中輔政一紀，年益高。

translations.literal: He Zhizhong had assisted in governance for twelve years, and his age was advancing.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhizhong had assisted in governance for twelve years, and his age was advancing.

sentences.zh: 五年，臥疾甚，賜寬告。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he fell gravely ill and was granted extended leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he fell gravely ill and was granted extended leave.

sentences.zh: 他日造朝，命止赴六參起居，退治省事。

translations.literal: On another day he came to court; he was ordered to attend only the six monthly audiences and then retire to handle routine business.
translations.idiomatic: On another day he came to court. He was ordered to attend only the six monthly audiences and then retire to handle routine business.

sentences.zh: 明年，乃以太傅就第，許朝朔望，儀物廩稍，一切如居位時。

translations.literal: The next year he retired to his residence as Grand Tutor, permitted to attend court on the first and fifteenth of each month; ritual objects, stipends, and provisions were all as when he held office.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he retired to his residence as Grand Tutor, permitted to attend court on the first and fifteenth of each month. Ritual objects, stipends, and provisions were all as when he held office.

sentences.zh: 入見，帝曰：「自相位致為臣，數十年無此矣。

translations.literal: On entering audience, the emperor said: Since leaving the chancellorship to become a retired minister — for decades there has been nothing like this.
translations.idiomatic: On entering audience, the emperor said: "Since leaving the chancellorship to become a retired minister — for decades there has been nothing like this."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「昔張士遜亦以舊學際遇，用太傅致仕，與臣適同。

translations.literal: He replied: In the past Zhang Shizun likewise, by virtue of his classical learning, was granted retirement as Grand Tutor — the same as your subject.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "In the past Zhang Shizun likewise, by virtue of his classical learning, was granted retirement as Grand Tutor — the same as your subject."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「當時恩禮，恐未必爾。

translations.literal: The emperor said: The favor and ceremony of that time, I fear, were not necessarily like this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The favor and ceremony of that time, I fear, were not necessarily like this."

sentences.zh: 」執中頓首謝。

translations.literal: He Zhizhong kowtowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhizhong kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 其在政府，嘗戒邊吏勿生事，重改作，惜人材，寬民力。

translations.literal: While in government he often warned border officials not to provoke incidents, valued restraint in construction, cherished human talent, and lightened burdens on the people.
translations.idiomatic: While in government he often warned border officials not to provoke incidents, valued restraint in construction, cherished human talent, and lightened burdens on the people.

sentences.zh: 雖居富貴，未嘗忘貧賤時。

translations.literal: Though he lived in wealth and honor, he never forgot his days of poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Though he lived in wealth and honor, he never forgot his days of poverty.

sentences.zh: 斥緡錢萬置義莊，以贍宗族。

translations.literal: He spent ten thousand strings of cash to establish a charity estate to support his clan.
translations.idiomatic: He spent ten thousand strings of cash to establish a charity estate to support his clan.

sentences.zh: 性復謹畏，至於迎順主意，贊飾太平，則始終一致，不能自克。

translations.literal: By nature he was also cautious and timid; in deferring to the sovereign's wishes and embellishing the age of peace, he was consistent from first to last and could not restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was also cautious and timid. In deferring to the sovereign's wishes and embellishing the age of peace, he was consistent from first to last and could not restrain himself.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died, aged seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 帝即幸其家，以不及視其病為恨，輟視朝三日，贈太師，追封清源郡王，諡曰「正獻」。

translations.literal: The emperor at once visited his home, regretting that he had not been able to see him during his illness; court audiences were suspended for three days. He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qingyuan, and given the epithet Zhengxian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once visited his home, regretting that he had not been able to see him during his illness. Court audiences were suspended for three days. He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qingyuan, and given the epithet Zhengxian.

translations.literal: Zheng Juzhong
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Juzhong

translations.idiomatic: Zheng Juzhong, style name Dafu, was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 登進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，為都官禮部員外郎，起居舍人，至中書舍人、直學士院。

translations.literal: During Chongning he served as vice director in the Ministries of Justice and Rites, diarist, and eventually drafting secretary and academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During Chongning he served as vice director in the Ministries of Justice and Rites, diarist, and eventually drafting secretary and academician of the Hanlin Academy.

translations.idiomatic: At first Juzhong claimed to be a cousin of the imperial consort. The consort had risen from the princely household with a humble family background and also relied on Juzhong for support. By this means he received successive promotions.

translations.literal: It happened that the consort's father Shen had a guest Zhu Anzhong who submitted a memorial involving slander; memorialists implicated Juzhong as well. He was dismissed and made prefect of Hezhou, then transferred to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the consort's father Shen had a guest Zhu Anzhong who submitted a memorial involving slander. Memorialists implicated Juzhong as well. He was dismissed and made prefect of Hezhou, then transferred to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，歸故官，遷給事中、翰林學士。

translations.literal: The next year he was restored to his former post and promoted to supervisory censor and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was restored to his former post and promoted to supervisory censor and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，同知樞密院。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan he became vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daguan he became vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時妃寵冠後宮，於居中無所賴，乃用宦官黃經臣策，以外戚秉政辭。

translations.literal: At the time the consort's favor surpassed all in the inner palace; she no longer relied on Juzhong and adopted the eunuch Huang Jingchen's stratagem, declining office on grounds of being a maternal relative holding power.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the consort's favor surpassed all in the inner palace. She no longer relied on Juzhong and adopted the eunuch Huang Jingchen's stratagem, declining office on grounds of being a maternal relative holding power.

sentences.zh: 改資政學士、中太一宮使兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was changed to academician of the Hall of Literary Glory, commissioner of the Zhongtaiyi Palace, and concurrent reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to academician of the Hall of Literary Glory, commissioner of the Zhongtaiyi Palace, and concurrent reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 蔡京以星文變免，趙挺之相，與劉逵謀盡改京所為政。

translations.literal: Cai Jing was dismissed because of celestial anomalies; Zhao Tingzhi became chancellor and with Liu Kui plotted to overturn entirely the policies Cai Jing had enacted.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing was dismissed because of celestial anomalies. Zhao Tingzhi became chancellor and, with Liu Kui, plotted to overturn entirely the policies Cai Jing had enacted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徽宗頗悔更張之暴，外莫有知者。

translations.literal: Before long Huizong came to regret the violence of the reversal, but no one outside knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Huizong came to regret the violence of the reversal, but no one outside knew of it.

sentences.zh: 居中往來紳所，知之，即入見言：「陛下建學校、興禮樂，以藻飾太平；

translations.literal: Juzhong visited Shen's residence and learned of this; he at once entered audience and said: Your Majesty has established schools and revived rites and music to adorn an age of peace;
translations.idiomatic: Juzhong visited Shen's residence and learned of this. He at once entered audience and said: "Your Majesty has established schools and revived rites and music to adorn an age of peace;

sentences.zh: 置居養、安濟院，以周拯窮困，何所逆天而致威譴乎？

translations.literal: established residential care and relief hospices to succor the destitute — in what way have you offended Heaven to incur such awesome reproof?
translations.idiomatic: established residential care and relief hospices to succor the destitute. In what way have you offended Heaven to incur such awesome reproof?"

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly enlightened.

sentences.zh: 居中退語禮部侍郎劉正夫，正夫繼請對，語同。

translations.literal: Juzhong withdrew and spoke with Vice Minister of Rites Liu Zhengfu; Zhengfu then requested audience and spoke similarly.
translations.idiomatic: Juzhong withdrew and spoke with Vice Minister of Rites Liu Zhengfu. Zhengfu then requested audience and spoke similarly.

sentences.zh: 帝意乃復向京。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind then turned back toward Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind then turned back toward Jing.

sentences.zh: 京再得政，兩人之助為多。

translations.literal: When Jing regained power, the help of these two men was considerable.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing regained power, the help of these two men was considerable.

sentences.zh: 居中厚責報，京為言樞密本兵之地，與三省殊，無嫌於用親。

translations.literal: Juzhong pressed hard for reward. Jing argued that the Bureau of Military Affairs was fundamentally a military post, distinct from the Three Departments, and there was no objection to employing a relative.
translations.idiomatic: Juzhong pressed hard for reward. Jing argued that the Bureau of Military Affairs was fundamentally a military post, distinct from the Three Departments, and there was no objection to employing a relative.

translations.literal: Jingchen was then relying on power and forcefully resisted the earlier proposal; Jing's words had no effect.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchen was then relying on power and forcefully resisted the earlier proposal. Jing's words had no effect.

sentences.zh: 居中疑不己援，始怨之，乃與張康國比而間京。

translations.literal: Juzhong suspected he was not being supported and began to resent Jing; he then allied with Zhang Kangguo to sow discord against him.
translations.idiomatic: Juzhong suspected he was not being supported and began to resent Jing. He then allied with Zhang Kangguo to sow discord against him.

sentences.zh: 都水使者趙霖得龜兩首於黃河，獻以為瑞。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Capital Waterways Zhao Lin obtained a two-headed turtle from the Yellow River and presented it as an auspicious omen.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of the Capital Waterways Zhao Lin obtained a two-headed turtle from the Yellow River and presented it as an auspicious omen.

sentences.zh: 京曰：「此齊小白所謂『象罔』，見之而霸者也。

translations.literal: Jing said: This is what Duke Huan of Qi called Xiangwang — seeing it, one achieves hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said: "This is what Duke Huan of Qi called Xiangwang — seeing it, one achieves hegemony."

translations.literal: Juzhong said: How can a head properly have two?
translations.idiomatic: Juzhong said: "How can a head properly have two?

sentences.zh: 人皆駭異，而京獨主之，殆不可測。

translations.literal: Everyone was alarmed and astonished, yet Jing alone upheld it — his intentions were perhaps beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone was alarmed and astonished, yet Jing alone upheld it. His intentions were perhaps beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 」帝命棄龜金明池，謂：「居中愛我」，遂申前命，進知院事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the turtle discarded in Jinming Pool and said: Juzhong loves me — and then confirmed the earlier appointment, promoting him to commissioner of the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the turtle discarded in Jinming Pool and said: "Juzhong loves me." He then confirmed the earlier appointment, promoting him to commissioner of the bureau.

sentences.zh: 四年，京又罷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Jing was dismissed again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Jing was dismissed again.

sentences.zh: 居中自許必得相，而帝覺之，不用。

translations.literal: Juzhong assured himself he would surely become chancellor, but the emperor perceived this and did not appoint him.
translations.idiomatic: Juzhong assured himself he would surely become chancellor, but the emperor perceived this and did not appoint him.

sentences.zh: 妃正位中宮，復以嫌，罷為觀文殿學士。

translations.literal: When the consort took her proper place in the inner palace, he was again dismissed on grounds of impropriety and made academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature.
translations.idiomatic: When the consort took her proper place in the inner palace, he was again dismissed on grounds of impropriety and made academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature.

sentences.zh: 政和中，再知樞密院，官累特進。

translations.literal: During Zhenghe he again became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, cumulatively reaching specially advanced rank.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenghe he again became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, cumulatively reaching specially advanced rank.

sentences.zh: 時京總治三省，益變亂法度。

translations.literal: At the time Jing controlled all Three Departments and further altered and disrupted laws and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jing controlled all Three Departments and further altered and disrupted laws and institutions.

sentences.zh: 居中每為帝言，帝亦惡京專，尋拜居中少保、太宰，使伺察之。

translations.literal: Juzhong often spoke to the emperor about this; the emperor also detested Jing's monopoly of power. Soon Juzhong was appointed Junior Guardian and Grand Chancellor and charged to keep watch on him.
translations.idiomatic: Juzhong often spoke to the emperor about this. The emperor also detested Jing's monopoly of power. Soon Juzhong was appointed Junior Guardian and Grand Chancellor and charged to keep watch on him.

sentences.zh: 居中存紀綱，守格令，抑僥幸，振淹滯，士論翕然望治。

translations.literal: Juzhong preserved discipline, upheld regulations, restrained undue favor-seeking, and revived the stalled; scholarly opinion united in hope of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Juzhong preserved discipline, upheld regulations, restrained undue favor-seeking, and revived the stalled. Scholarly opinion united in hope of good governance.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，旋詔起復。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his mother, he was soon recalled by edict before mourning ended.
translations.idiomatic: Upon mourning for his mother, he was soon recalled by edict before mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 逾年，加少傅，得請終喪。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was promoted to Junior Tutor and granted permission to complete his mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was promoted to Junior Tutor and granted permission to complete his mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，以威武軍節度使使佑神觀。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was made military commissioner of Weiwu Circuit and commissioner of the Youshen Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was made military commissioner of Weiwu Circuit and commissioner of the Youshen Palace.

sentences.zh: 還領樞密院，加少師。

translations.literal: He returned to head the Bureau of Military Affairs and was promoted to Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to head the Bureau of Military Affairs and was promoted to Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 連封崇、宿、燕三國公。

translations.literal: He was successively enfeoffed as Duke of Chong, Duke of Su, and Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively enfeoffed as Duke of Chong, Duke of Su, and Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣使與金約夾攻契丹，復燕雲，蔡京、童貫主之。

translations.literal: The court dispatched envoys to agree with Jin on a pincer attack against the Khitan to recover Yan-Yun; Cai Jing and Tong Guan directed the effort.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched envoys to agree with Jin on a pincer attack against the Khitan to recover Yan-Yun. Cai Jing and Tong Guan directed the effort.

translations.idiomatic: Juzhong forcefully argued against it and said to Jing: "You are a great minister,

translations.idiomatic: They did not listen.

translations.idiomatic: When Yanshan was pacified, he was promoted to Grand Guardian. Declaring he had no merit, he declined to accept.

sentences.zh: 入朝，暴遇疾歸舍，數日卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: On entering court he suddenly fell ill, returned home, and died within days, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: On entering court he suddenly fell ill, returned home, and died within days, aged sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太師、華原郡王，諡「文正」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and Prince of Huayuan, with the epithet Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and Prince of Huayuan, with the epithet Wenzheng.

translations.literal: The emperor personally inscribed his tomb stele: Tomb of Wenzheng Zheng Juzhong, the pure Confucian chancellor of Zhenghe's bright reign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally inscribed his tomb stele: "Tomb of Wenzheng Zheng Juzhong, the pure Confucian chancellor of Zhenghe's bright reign."

sentences.zh: 居中始仕，蔡京即薦其有廊廟器。

translations.literal: When Juzhong first entered office, Cai Jing at once recommended him as having the makings of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Juzhong first entered office, Cai Jing at once recommended him as having the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 既不合，遂因蔡渭理其父確功狀，追治王珪。

translations.literal: When they fell out, he then used Cai Wei to review the record of his father Que's merits and pursued punishment against Wang Gui.
translations.idiomatic: When they fell out, he then used Cai Wei to review the record of his father Que's merits and pursued punishment against Wang Gui.

sentences.zh: 居中，珪婿也，故借是撼之，然卒不能害。

translations.literal: Juzhong was Wang Gui's son-in-law and thus used this to shake him, yet in the end could not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Juzhong was Wang Gui's son-in-law and thus used this to shake him, yet in the end could not harm him.

sentences.zh: 子修年、億年，皆至侍從。

translations.literal: His sons Xiunian and Yinian both reached positions as palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xiunian and Yinian both reached positions as palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 億年遭靖康之難，沒入於金。

translations.literal: Yinian suffered the calamity of Jingkang and was taken captive by Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yinian suffered the calamity of Jingkang and was taken captive by Jin.

sentences.zh: 後遣事劉豫，晚得南歸，秦檜以婦氏親擢為資政殿大學士，位視執正。

translations.literal: Later he was sent to serve Liu Yu; in his later years he returned south. Qin Hui, as a relative by marriage, promoted him to Grand Master of the Hall of Literary Glory with rank equal to a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was sent to serve Liu Yu. In his later years he returned south. Qin Hui, as a relative by marriage, promoted him to Grand Master of the Hall of Literary Glory with rank equal to a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 檜死，亦竄死撫州。

translations.literal: When Hui died, he too was banished and died in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui died, he too was banished and died in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時又有安堯臣者，亦嘗上書論燕雲之事，其言曰：

translations.literal: At the time there was also An Yaochen, who had submitted a memorial on the Yan-Yun question; his words ran:
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was also An Yaochen, who had submitted a memorial on the Yan-Yun question. His words ran:

sentences.zh: 「宦寺專命，倡為大謀，燕雲之役興，則邊釁遂開；

translations.literal: When eunuchs monopolize command and advocate grand schemes, once the Yan-Yun campaign begins, border conflicts are opened;
translations.idiomatic: "When eunuchs monopolize command and advocate grand schemes, once the Yan-Yun campaign begins, border conflicts are opened;

sentences.zh: 宦寺之權重，則皇綱不振。

translations.literal: when eunuch power grows heavy, the imperial order is not upheld.
translations.idiomatic: when eunuch power grows heavy, the imperial order is not upheld.

sentences.zh: 昔秦始皇築長城，漢武帝通西域，隋煬帝遼左之師，唐明皇幽薊之寇，其失如彼。

translations.literal: In the past Qin Shihuang built the Long Wall, Han Wudi opened the Western Regions, Sui Yangdi's campaign in Liaodong, and Tang Minghuang's incursion at Youji — their failures were like those.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Qin Shihuang built the Long Wall, Han Wudi opened the Western Regions, Sui Yangdi's campaign in Liaodong, and Tang Minghuang's incursion at Youji — their failures were like those.

sentences.zh: 周宣王伐玁狁，漢文帝備北邊，元帝納賈捐之之議，光武斥臧宮、馬武之謀，其得如此。

translations.literal: King Xuan of Zhou campaigned against the Xianyun, Han Wendi prepared the northern frontier, Yuandi accepted Jia Juanzhi's proposal, and Guangwu rejected the schemes of Zang Gong and Ma Wu — their successes were like these.
translations.idiomatic: King Xuan of Zhou campaigned against the Xianyun, Han Wendi prepared the northern frontier, Yuandi accepted Jia Juanzhi's proposal, and Guangwu rejected the schemes of Zang Gong and Ma Wu — their successes were like these.

sentences.zh: 藝祖撥亂反正，躬擐甲胄，當時將相大臣，皆所與取天下者，豈勇略智力，不能下幽燕哉？

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu restored order from chaos and personally donned armor; the generals and chief ministers of that time were all those who had taken the realm with him — could their courage, strategy, and intelligence not have subdued You-Yan?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu restored order from chaos and personally donned armor. The generals and chief ministers of that time were all those who had taken the realm with him — could their courage, strategy, and intelligence not have subdued You-Yan?

sentences.zh: 蓋以區區之地，契丹所必爭，忍使吾民重困鋒鏑！

translations.literal: It was because that narrow territory was what the Khitan would surely contest — how could he bear to let our people again suffer under sword and spear!
translations.idiomatic: It was because that narrow territory was what the Khitan would surely contest — how could he bear to let our people again suffer under sword and spear!

sentences.zh: 章聖澶淵之役，與之戰而勝，乃聽其和，亦欲固本而息民也。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhensong at the Chanyuan campaign fought and won, then accepted peace — likewise wishing to secure the foundation and give the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhensong at the Chanyuan campaign fought and won, then accepted peace — likewise wishing to secure the foundation and give the people rest.

sentences.zh: 今童貫深結蔡京，同納趙良嗣以為謀主，故建平燕之議。

translations.literal: Now Tong Guan is deeply allied with Cai Jing and together they have taken in Zhao Liangsi as chief strategist — hence the proposal to pacify Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Now Tong Guan is deeply allied with Cai Jing and together they have taken in Zhao Liangsi as chief strategist — hence the proposal to pacify Yan.

sentences.zh: 臣恐異時唇亡齒寒，邊境有可乘之釁，狼子蓄銳，伺隙以逞其欲，此臣所以日夜寒心。

translations.literal: Your subject fears that in time, when the lips are gone the teeth grow cold — when the border offers an opening for exploitation, the wolf cub stores its sharpness and watches for a gap to indulge its desires. This is why your subject's heart is chilled day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject fears that in time, when the lips are gone the teeth grow cold — when the border offers an opening for exploitation, the wolf cub stores its sharpness and watches for a gap to indulge its desires. This is why your subject's heart is chilled day and night.

sentences.zh: 伏望思祖宗積累之艱難，鑒歷代君臣之得失，杜塞邊隙，務守舊好，無使外夷乘間窺中國，上以安宗廟，下以慰生靈。」

translations.literal: I humbly pray Your Majesty will reflect on the hardships through which our ancestors accumulated the realm, take warning from the gains and losses of rulers and ministers through the ages, block border openings, strive to maintain the old friendship, and not let foreign barbarians seize an interval to spy on China — above to secure the ancestral temples, below to comfort the living.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray Your Majesty will reflect on the hardships through which our ancestors accumulated the realm, take warning from the gains and losses of rulers and ministers through the ages, block border openings, strive to maintain the old friendship, and not let foreign barbarians seize an interval to spy on China — above to secure the ancestral temples, below to comfort the living."

sentences.zh: 徽宗然之，命堯臣以官；

translations.literal: Huizong approved and ordered Yaochen granted an office;
translations.idiomatic: Huizong approved and ordered Yaochen granted an office;

sentences.zh: 後竟為姦謀所奪。

translations.literal: later it was ultimately seized away by treacherous schemers.
translations.idiomatic: later it was ultimately seized away by treacherous schemers.

sentences.zh: 堯臣嘗舉進士不第，蓋惇之族子也。

translations.literal: Yaochen had attempted the jinshi examination without success; he was a clansman of Zhang Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Yaochen had attempted the jinshi examination without success. He was a clansman of Zhang Dun.

sentences.zh: 論曰：君子小人，猶冰炭不可一日而處者也。

translations.literal: The commentators say: The noble man and the petty man are like ice and charcoal — they cannot abide together for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: The noble man and the petty man are like ice and charcoal — they cannot abide together for a single day.

sentences.zh: 趙挺之為小官，薄有才具，熙寧新法之行，迎合用事，元祐更化，宜為諸賢鄙棄。

translations.literal: Zhao Tingzhi as a minor official had modest talent; when the New Policies of Xining were implemented he curried favor with those in power — at the Yuanyou reversal he ought to have been despised and cast aside by the worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingzhi as a minor official had modest talent. When the New Policies of Xining were implemented he curried favor with those in power — at the Yuanyou reversal he ought to have been despised and cast aside by the worthies.

sentences.zh: 至於紹聖，首倡紹述之謀，牴排正人，靡所不至。

translations.literal: By the Shaosheng era he was first to advocate the plan of continuing the late emperor's policies, driving out upright men by every means imaginable.
translations.idiomatic: By the Shaosheng era he was first to advocate the plan of continuing the late emperor's policies, driving out upright men by every means imaginable.

sentences.zh: 其論蔡京，不過為攘奪權寵之計而已，所謂「楚固為失，齊亦未為得」也。

translations.literal: His attacks on Cai Jing were nothing but a scheme to seize power and favor — as the saying goes, Chu was indeed in the wrong, but Qi was not necessarily in the right either.
translations.idiomatic: His attacks on Cai Jing were nothing but a scheme to seize power and favor — as the saying goes, Chu was indeed in the wrong, but Qi was not necessarily in the right either.

sentences.zh: 徽宗知京不可顓任，乃以張商英、鄭居中輩敢與京為異者參而用之。

translations.literal: Huizong knew Jing could not be entrusted with sole power and therefore employed alongside him men like Zhang Shangying and Zheng Juzhong who dared differ with Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong knew Jing could not be entrusted with sole power and therefore employed alongside him men like Zhang Shangying and Zheng Juzhong who dared differ with Jing.

sentences.zh: 殊不知二人者，向背離合，視利所在，亦何有於公議哉？

translations.literal: He little realized that these two men shifted allegiance according to where advantage lay — what regard had they for public opinion?
translations.idiomatic: He little realized that these two men shifted allegiance according to where advantage lay — what regard had they for public opinion?

sentences.zh: 商英以傾詖之行，竊忠直之名，沒齒猶見褒稱，其欺世如此！

translations.literal: Shangying by treacherous conduct stole a reputation for integrity and uprightness; even to the end of his days he was praised — such was his deception of the world!
translations.idiomatic: Shangying by treacherous conduct stole a reputation for integrity and uprightness. Even to the end of his days he was praised — such was his deception of the world!

sentences.zh: 何執中夤緣舊學，致位兩府，無所建明，惟務冒嫉，至用石悈脅陳瓘取《尊堯集》，欲因以殺瓘，何為者耶？

translations.literal: He Zhizhong climbed by connections through the old learning faction to reach the Two Departments, offered no constructive proposals, and devoted himself only to reckless envy — even using Shi Jie to coerce Chen Guan into surrendering Respect for Yao, intending thereby to kill Guan. What was he about?
translations.idiomatic: He Zhizhong climbed by connections through the old learning faction to reach the Two Departments, offered no constructive proposals, and devoted himself only to reckless envy — even using Shi Jie to coerce Chen Guan into surrendering Respect for Yao, intending thereby to kill Guan. What was he about?

sentences.zh: 宣、政命相，得若而人，尚望治乎？

translations.literal: In the Xuanhe and Zhenghe eras, chancellors appointed were men like these — could one still hope for good governance?
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanhe and Zhenghe eras, chancellors appointed were men like these — could one still hope for good governance?

sentences.zh: 劉正夫生平所為，睒申出沒正邪之間，商英之徒也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhengfu's conduct throughout his life flickered in and out between the upright and the corrupt — he was of Shangying's kind.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengfu's conduct throughout his life flickered in and out between the upright and the corrupt — he was of Shangying's kind.

sentences.zh: 唐英有清才而寡失德，獨薦王安石為可咎；

translations.literal: Tang Ying had pure talent and few moral failings; only his recommendation of Wang Anshi is open to reproach;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Ying had pure talent and few moral failings. Only his recommendation of Wang Anshi is open to reproach;

sentences.zh: 然安石未相，正人端士孰不與之，又何責乎唐英！

translations.literal: yet before Anshi became chancellor, which upright and principled man did not associate with him? Why then blame Tang Ying!
translations.idiomatic: yet before Anshi became chancellor, which upright and principled man did not associate with him? Why then blame Tang Ying!

sentences.zh: 張康國

translations.literal: Zhang Kangguo
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kangguo

sentences.zh: 始因蔡京進，京定元祐黨籍，看詳講議司，編彙章牘，皆預密議，故汲汲引援之，帝亦器重焉。

translations.literal: At first he advanced through Cai Jing's patronage. When Jing fixed the Yuanyou faction register, the Review and Deliberation Office, and the compilation of memorials, Kangguo took part in all secret deliberations; Jing therefore eagerly promoted him, and the emperor also valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: At first he advanced through Cai Jing's patronage. When Jing fixed the Yuanyou faction register, the Review and Deliberation Office, and the compilation of memorials, Kangguo took part in all secret deliberations. Jing therefore eagerly promoted him, and the emperor also valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 及得志，浸為崖異。

translations.literal: Once he achieved his ambitions, he gradually became estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Once he achieved his ambitions, he gradually became estranged.

sentences.zh: 帝惡京專愎，陰令沮其姦，嘗許以相。

translations.literal: The emperor detested Jing's monopoly and obstinacy and secretly ordered Kangguo to obstruct his schemes; he once promised him the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor detested Jing's monopoly and obstinacy and secretly ordered Kangguo to obstruct his schemes. He once promised him the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 是時，西北邊帥多取部內好官自辟置，以力不以才。

translations.literal: At the time northwestern frontier commanders often selected favored officials within their jurisdictions for appointment by personal recommendation, by influence rather than talent.
translations.idiomatic: At the time northwestern frontier commanders often selected favored officials within their jurisdictions for appointment by personal recommendation, by influence rather than talent.

sentences.zh: 康國曰：「並塞當擇人以紓憂顧，奈何欲私所善乎？

translations.literal: Kangguo said: Along the border we ought to select men to relieve anxieties and concerns — how can you wish to favor your private choices?
translations.idiomatic: Kangguo said: "Along the border we ought to select men to relieve anxieties and concerns. How can you wish to favor your private choices?

sentences.zh: 」乃隨闕選用，定為格。

translations.literal: He then filled vacancies as they arose and established this as a standard.
translations.idiomatic: He then filled vacancies as they arose and established this as a standard."

sentences.zh: 京使御史中丞吳執中擊康國，康國先知之。

translations.literal: Jing had Censor-in-Chief Wu Zhizhong attack Kangguo; Kangguo learned of it beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had Censor-in-Chief Wu Zhizhong attack Kangguo. Kangguo learned of it beforehand.

sentences.zh: 旦奏事，留白帝曰：「執中今日入對，必為京論臣，臣願辟位。

translations.literal: At the morning audience he remained behind and told the emperor: Zhizhong will enter audience today and will surely speak on Jing's behalf against your subject. I wish to yield my post.
translations.idiomatic: At the morning audience he remained behind and told the emperor: "Zhizhong will enter audience today and will surely speak on Jing's behalf against your subject. I wish to yield my post."

sentences.zh: 」既而執中對，果陳其事，帝叱去之。

translations.literal: When Zhizhong entered audience, he indeed presented the matter; the emperor shouted him away.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhizhong entered audience, he indeed presented the matter. The emperor shouted him away.

sentences.zh: 他日，康國因朝退，趨殿廬，暴得疾，仰天吐舌，舁至待漏院卒，或疑中毒云。

translations.literal: On another day, as court was dismissed, Kangguo hurried toward the palace offices and suddenly fell ill, staring skyward with tongue protruding; he was carried to the Waiting-for-Dawn Court and died there. Some suspected poisoning.
translations.idiomatic: On another day, as court was dismissed, Kangguo hurried toward the palace offices and suddenly fell ill, staring skyward with tongue protruding. He was carried to the Waiting-for-Dawn Court and died there. Some suspected poisoning.

sentences.zh: 年五十四。

translations.literal: He was aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was aged fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，諡曰「文簡」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Honorary Grand Master with ceremonials equal to the Three Excellencies, with the epithet Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Honorary Grand Master with ceremonials equal to the Three Excellencies, with the epithet Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 康伯，仕終吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His son Kangbo ended his career as minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kangbo ended his career as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 朱諤，字聖與，秀州華亭人，初名𥿈。

translations.literal: Zhu E, style name Shengyu, a native of Huating in Xiu Prefecture; his original name was Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu E, style name Shengyu, was a native of Huating in Xiu Prefecture. His original name was Zhu.

sentences.zh: 進士第二，調忠正軍推官。

translations.literal: He placed second in the jinshi examination and was appointed legal officer in Zhongzheng Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He placed second in the jinshi examination and was appointed legal officer in Zhongzheng Circuit.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初，由太常丞擢殿中侍御史，遷侍御史、給事中。

translations.literal: At the start of Chongning he was promoted from vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to palace censor, then transferred to censor and supervisory memorial reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Chongning he was promoted from vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to palace censor, then transferred to censor and supervisory memorial reviewer.

sentences.zh: 以同黨籍人姓名，故改名。

translations.literal: Because his name matched that of someone on the faction register, he changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: Because his name matched that of someone on the faction register, he changed his name.

sentences.zh: 進御史中丞，入謝，徽宗曰：「今朝廷肅清，上下無事，宜審重以稱朕意。

translations.literal: Promoted to censor-in-chief, on entering to give thanks Huizong said: The court is now orderly and all is quiet above and below. You ought to be careful and weighty to suit my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to censor-in-chief, on entering to give thanks Huizong said: "The court is now orderly and all is quiet above and below. You ought to be careful and weighty to suit my intent."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「前此中執法類不知職守，言事多妄，至過天津橋，見汴堤一角墊陷，乞修葺。

translations.literal: He replied: Previously censors in this office generally did not know their duties; their memorials were mostly reckless — even passing the Tianjin Bridge and seeing a corner of the Bian embankment sunken, they would request repairs.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Previously censors in this office generally did not know their duties. Their memorials were mostly reckless — even passing the Tianjin Bridge and seeing a corner of the Bian embankment sunken, they would request repairs.

sentences.zh: 如許細故，何足論哉？

translations.literal: Such trivial matters — what are they worth discussing?
translations.idiomatic: Such trivial matters — what are they worth discussing?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: True.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "True.

sentences.zh: 比石豫、許敦仁妄發，皆如是。

translations.literal: Recently Shi Yu and Xu Dunren made reckless submissions — all like this.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Shi Yu and Xu Dunren made reckless submissions — all like this."

sentences.zh: 」諤遂奏：「願如神宗故事，聽政之餘，開內閣，延群臣，從容論道。」

translations.literal: E then memorialized: I pray that, following Emperor Shenzong's precedent, after handling affairs of state Your Majesty will open the inner cabinet, summon the ministers, and at leisure discuss the Way.
translations.idiomatic: E then memorialized: "I pray that, following Emperor Shenzong's precedent, after handling affairs of state Your Majesty will open the inner cabinet, summon the ministers, and at leisure discuss the Way."

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下手詔屢下，惻怛願治。

translations.literal: He also said: Your Majesty's handwritten edicts have been issued repeatedly, filled with compassionate desire for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Your Majesty's handwritten edicts have been issued repeatedly, filled with compassionate desire for good governance.

sentences.zh: 然吏奉行者多安於苟簡，或懷二三，柅置不行，使德音善教，無由下達。

translations.literal: Yet officials who carry them out mostly rest content with perfunctory compliance, or harbor reservations and obstruct implementation, so that benevolent words and good instruction cannot reach below.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials who carry them out mostly rest content with perfunctory compliance, or harbor reservations and obstruct implementation, so that benevolent words and good instruction cannot reach below.

sentences.zh: 願分命使者刺舉諸道，有受令而不行及行令而不盡者，論如古留令、虧令之罪，則令出而朝廷尊矣。

translations.literal: I pray that envoys be dispatched to investigate the circuits; those who receive orders but do not execute them, or execute them incompletely, should be punished as in ancient times for retaining or impairing orders — then when orders issue forth the court will be honored.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that envoys be dispatched to investigate the circuits. Those who receive orders but do not execute them, or execute them incompletely, should be punished as in ancient times for retaining or impairing orders — then when orders issue forth the court will be honored.

sentences.zh: 元祐紛更，凡得罪於熙寧、元豐者，不問是否，輒陳冤訴，自歸無過之地，彰先朝之失刑，希合姦臣，規求進用。

translations.literal: During the Yuanyou reversal, all who had offended in the Xining and Yuanfeng eras, regardless of guilt, hastened to plead injustice, declaring themselves blameless, exposing the prior court's errors in punishment, currying favor with treacherous ministers, and scheming for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou reversal, all who had offended in the Xining and Yuanfeng eras, regardless of guilt, hastened to plead injustice, declaring themselves blameless, exposing the prior court's errors in punishment, currying favor with treacherous ministers, and scheming for advancement.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎許將頃下御史獄，抗章云：「絲毫自知其無事，父子相係而為囚，追屬吏十有六人，繫病者百有三日，終無可坐之罪，遂加不實之刑。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Chancellery Xu Jiang was recently sent to the censorial prison and submitted a defiant memorial saying: I know to the smallest degree that I am innocent. Father and son were bound together as prisoners; sixteen subordinate officials were pursued; the sick were detained for a hundred and three days — in the end there was no crime to be found, yet false punishment was imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Chancellery Xu Jiang was recently sent to the censorial prison and submitted a defiant memorial saying: "I know to the smallest degree that I am innocent. Father and son were bound together as prisoners. Sixteen subordinate officials were pursued. The sick were detained for a hundred and three days — in the end there was no crime to be found, yet false punishment was imposed.

sentences.zh: 」夫以追屬吏如是之多，繫病者如是之久，卒之於無可坐，則先帝所用之刑為何哉？

translations.literal: If so many subordinates were pursued and the sick detained so long, yet in the end there was nothing to punish — then what were the punishments employed by the late emperor?
translations.idiomatic: If so many subordinates were pursued and the sick detained so long, yet in the end there was nothing to punish — then what were the punishments employed by the late emperor?

sentences.zh: 將於哲廟表，泛為平詞；

translations.literal: Before Emperor Zhezong's tablet he spoke in general and neutral terms;
translations.idiomatic: Before Emperor Zhezong's tablet he spoke in general and neutral terms;

sentences.zh: 至宣仁太后之前，則銜冤負痛。

translations.literal: before Empress Dowager Xuanren he bore grievance and pain.
translations.idiomatic: before Empress Dowager Xuanren he bore grievance and pain.

sentences.zh: 其辭如此，於陛下紹述成功，得無少損乎？

translations.literal: His words being such, does this not somewhat diminish Your Majesty's success in continuing the late emperor's policies?
translations.idiomatic: His words being such, does this not somewhat diminish Your Majesty's success in continuing the late emperor's policies?"

sentences.zh: 侯蒙逮治五路將帥，力為申理，十八人者繇之而免，其仁人利溥之言乎？

translations.literal: Hou Meng arrested and tried the commanders of five routes yet forcefully pleaded their case — the eighteen men were spared through him. Was this not the speech of a benevolent man whose benefit reaches far?
